#894. 'It's been horrific' - Evatt says sickness bug decimated Blackpool

Evatt: 'I've never seen anything like it'

Blackpool boss Ian Evatt has revealed his squad had a horrific build-up to their defeat by fellow League One strugglers AFC Wimbledon following a fast-spreading sickness bug in his camp.

The Seasiders were without 15 players and staff for Saturday's visit to the capital as they suffered from "severe diarrhoea and vomiting", with some suffering such symptoms when playing.

Evatt's side lost 1-0 at the Cherry Red Records Stadium - their seventh league defeat of the season - and are now 20th and only outside the bottom four on goal difference.

"There's some players and staff that haven't been able to to make it out of bed," Evatt told BBC Radio Lancashire.

"Some staff have had to continue to do their jobs with the vomiting and the diarrhoea and the players are the same - some players were vomiting on the pitch [or had] diarrhoea on the pitch. It's been horrific.

"I've got to be honest, I've never seen a virus spread so fast, I've never seen anything as aggressive as what it is."

Smith strike earns Wimbledon win over Blackpool

Evatt said the effects of the virus began by midday on Friday, the day before the fixture, and suspected its effects had its origins at their Squires Gate training facility.

Blackpool have now won just one game out of their past 10 League One fixtures with their opponents ending a poor run of form themselves, having not won in seven attempts prior to Saturday's fixture.

"We did everything we could, we followed every protocol we could, we followed every process, we separated players, we separated staff but it was continuing to spread," Evatt added.

"There's even staff that have had the virus that haven't even travelled with us so it's obviously something that's been picked up and started at Squires and it just snowballed fast.

"We did what we could in terms of following protocol and processes with what we were asked to do but obviously the game still went ahead and in my opinion it shouldn't have."

#893. Portugal immortalise Cristiano Ronaldo’s No 7 shirt in tribute to national legend

Original No 7 design preserved to honour player

Career brought 146 goals and three major titles

Portugal have made a permanent change to the No 7 shirt to honour the legacy of Cristiano Ronaldo and ensure the number remains forever associated with their greatest footballing icon.

The former forward, whose career spanned 23 years and 246 caps in which he scored 146 goals, announced his retirement on 5 November after a falling out with coach Jorge Jesus. His last appearance for Portugal was on 24 September, in a 1-0 home win over Wales in the Nations League.

Before their Nations League clash against Denmark, Portugal tweeted a unique design change to the iconic No 7 shirt to ensure Ronaldo’s version remains immortalised.

The small change to the number 7 is an acknowledgement of the star’s playing career in which he broke the men’s all-time scoring record. He captained his country to their first major trophy at Euro 2016, before adding two Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025.

Portugal will also pay tribute to Ronaldo before and during their Nations League fixture against Denmark in Braga on Saturday.

“Time to debut a new 7. Because there’s one that will be eternal,” the Portuguese national team wrote on social media on Saturday. The post included a goat emoji to signify “Greatest Of All Time”.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

It also included a video that showed a horizontal crossed line through the No 7 as it is commonly written in Europe, suggesting that Ronaldo’s successors will all have that cross to bear when they wear the number.

#892. How promotion, relegation and knockouts work in Nations League

England have reached the knockout rounds of the 2026-27 Uefa Nations League

Victory over Spain means England have finished top of Group A in the 2026-27 Nations group, sending them through to the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere in the home nations standings, Scotland still have the chance to finish second in Group B1 should they beat Switzerland on Tuesday - but would also need Slovenia to lose to North Macedonia.

Northern Ireland need only a draw away to Hungary to top Group B2 and advance to League A for the first time.

Wales are consigned to a bottom-place finish in Group A4, but could avoid relegation from the top tier if they win their relegation play-off in March.

Meanwhile the Republic of Ireland could still secure second place in Group B3 should they beat Kosovo.

November's international break is the final two full rounds of matches, with four rounds already completed in September and October.

The eight teams to finish in the top two of the four League A groups will play in the knockout rounds that start in March 2027.

Teams finishing at the top of groups in leagues B and C will earn promotion for the next Nations League cycle, while teams that finish second in a League B or League C group will face either a third-placed or bottom-placed team from the league above them in a promotion/relegation play-off.

The two worst sides to finish bottom of a League A group are automatically relegated. The other bottom sides in League A, third-placed sides in League A and bottom-placed sides in League B are at risk of relegation.

The losers of the play-offs will be relegated.

As the Nations League format is changing for the next cycle, taking place across 2028 and 2029, all League D teams are guaranteed promotion to League C.

Additionally, no teams from League C will be relegated at the end of this cycle.

The new format will consist of three larger leagues, meaning there will not be a League D in the next campaign.

Wales will finish bottom of their group and face a relegation play-off in March

The teams guaranteed to feature in the quarter-finals are:

â¢ Portugal (Group A4 qualifiers, final position TBC)

There is still another round of matches to go for groups A2, A4, B1, B2, B3 and B4, and some teams playing in groups C and below.

In Group A2. Netherlands and Greece are the top two, three points clear of Germany in third. With Serbia bottom on zero points, two of the current top three will advance.

In A4, Denmark are second and three points clear of Wales and Norway. One of the trio will join table-toppers Portugal.

The quarter-finals are played across two legs in March's international break.

The winners of each tie will advance to the semi-finals in June 2027, which are played in a one-off match across Wednesday 9 and Thursday 10 June. The final takes place on Sunday, 13 June.

Spain are the current holders of the European Championship, beating England in the 2024 final

Once the Nations League campaign is concluded, all 54 competing nations will be ranked based on their performance in this edition of the competition.

That ranking will have a direct impact on qualification for the 2028 European Championships, being held in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

The Nations League ranking will also determine the seeding of nations for Euro 2028 qualification.

Regular qualifying will take place between March and November 2027, with play-offs for the remaining spots in the tournament to take place in March 2028.

As there are four co-hosts and none of them have been granted immediate qualification, the number of how many qualify will effectively determine how many play-off spots will be up for grabs.

Uefa have said that up to two places will be given to the best-ranked co-hosts that fail to qualify for the tournament via its primary qualification route.

Scenarios have already been designed for occurrences where either two, one or zero co-hosts are given entry spots.

Depending on which play-off format is required, either eight or 12 teams will enter.

A total of 24 teams will enter the European Championships, 20 of them will consist of the winners of the 12 qualifying groups and the eight best runners-up from those group.

The remaining runners-up will enter the play-offs, alongside the Nations League group winners from League A, League B and League C that failed to finish in the top two of their Euro 2028 qualifying group.

If extra teams are required, the best-ranked League D group winner will enter the play-offs.

Any additional play-off spots that become available after that will filter down to the next-highest ranked Nations League finishers until the play-off spots are filled.

#891. Red Brawl New York: Fighting and six red cards mar ‘friendly’ v Club América

Game played without veterans and stars on both sides

One hallmark of Mauricio Pochettino’s time in international management has been his refusal to embrace the term “friendly”. His preferred branding is “unofficial games”.

His spin gained a bit of validity on Saturday, in the New York Red Bulls’ “friendly” against Club América, marred by a mass brawl between the sides that resulted in five red cards and a bevy of beverages thrown from the stands.

The game itself was odd for a few reasons. First, the Red Bulls have already been eliminated from MLS’s comically forgiving postseason, which means players (aside from veterans like Emil Forsberg) delayed vacations for a glorified scrimmage. Second, the match was announced on 1 October, at which point it was abundantly clear that the NWSL’s Gotham FC, a tenant of the Red Bulls’ Sports Illustrated Stadium, could host a playoff semi-final on the same weekend.

That scheduling snafu, combined with the comically poor state of the pitch, became a serious problem for the NWSL club, who settled for 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium for Sunday’s semi-final.

For the Red Bulls, the show must go on – and boy, did they find a way to entertain the fans who showed up for the low-stakes affair.

Not with their soccer exploits, mind you. Playing without the aforementioned veterans and US internationals Julian Hall and Adri Mehmeti, the remaining Red Bulls came ready for a scrap. At one point in the second half, América goalkeeper Rodolfo Cota required treatment for taking a boot above his knee while closing a shooting angle, putting the visitors on alert.

Roughly 40 minutes into the second half, this unofficial game abandoned any attempt to be friendly. Mijahir Jiménez dribbled toward the right corner flag, only to be taken down by a defender. He took great umbrage to the nature of the challenge, kicking off a maelstrom of shoves, punches, thrown drinks from the crowd, and men pressing their chests and foreheads together like bighorn rams in the throes of the rutting season.

The full sequence lives on thanks to a live watch-along streamed on YouTube, where former Mexico defender Miguel Layún comes to life in his gamer chair and begs his compatriots to keep the fracas alive. The fracas lasted 65 seconds, while the ensuing corner kick came a full seven minutes after Jimenez’s dribble.

The only scoreline from the night that matters: three Red Bulls sent off, three players from América, with the final five minutes being an eight-v-eight affair. The referee decided to forego any second half stoppage time, almost certainly for the best.

#890. British doubles No 1 criticises ATP bosses at trophy presentation absence

Henry Patten uses trophy presentation to focus on the absence of ATP bosses, reigniting his opposition to the doubles reform expected for 2028; You can watch the ATP Finals in Turin this week on Sky Sports Tennis

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

British doubles No 1 Henry Patten has taken a swipe at ATP bosses for their absence from a trophy presentation in Turin on Monday.

Upon receiving the year-end doubles No 1 trophy from chief tour officer Andre Silva, alongside his Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara, Patten called out the ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO Eno Polo.

"For us, it's a really big deal. It's a real shame that the ATP chairman and CEO don't think the same." Patten said.

"It would have been nice to have them on court with us today, but here we are by ourselves."

Sky Sports News has contacted the ATP Tour for comment.

Patten and Heliovaara enjoyed a sensational season, winning Wimbledon for the second time in their careers and lifting trophies in Adelaide, Doha, Dubai, and Madrid.

The duo have repeatedly criticised the ATP's approach to doubles, including their proposals that would include smaller draws and reduce prize money for the 2028 season.

Patten and Dutch player Sem Verbeek spearheaded an open letter, signed by over a hundred other players - including former champions Bob and Mike Bryan - calling for the reform project to be scrapped.

Speaking to Sky Sports Tennis, Tim Henman said: "He [Patten] made his thoughts pretty clear about the lack of representation from the chair and the CEO on the tour.

"There is the conversation around massive reform in the doubles world, potentially cutting the doubles draw in half and that would save prize money that could go into the singles, so those doubles players are feeling like their jobs are in jeopardy.

"This is a great platform as the doubles is getting incredible support."

Halving draw sizes. ATP Masters 1000 doubles draws would be cut in half to 16 teams, while smaller ATP 500 and 250 tournaments would drop to just eight teams Cutting prize money. The share of tournament prize money allocated to doubles would drop from 20% to 10%, shifting roughly $20 million (£15 million) away from doubles specialists to fund early-round singles payouts

Heliovaara also addressed the crowd, thanking Patten and their team, saying: "I'm going to say that Henry is the best partner in the world for doubles. I've been lucky enough to play with him for two and a half years.

"We shared a lot of wins, a lot of losses, but most of all, a lot of time everywhere in the world, really. On the court, off court, it's been a very nice, amazing trip together. But it's not just the two of us, I think it's also our team there in the box, in the spotlight today.

"I would like that we also give a big hand to every one of them. It's a lot of sacrifices from us, from the team, and obviously our families at home. Everybody who has helped us to achieve something like this. And to have a trophy like that at home, we will be very proud for a very long time."

Patten and Heliovaara will now turn their attention to the task at hand in Turin, where they are 1-0 in round-robin play. They defeated Orlando Luz and Rafael Matos in a match tie-break on Sunday.

#889. Ronaldinho makes comeback in Ravenna win

Ronaldinho played the first 45 minutes for Ravenna against Forli

Brazil legend Ronaldinho made his comeback aged 46 for Ravenna in their 2-0 win over Forli in an Italian third-tier derby.

The 46-year-old came out of retirement for the Serie C club he joined as an investor in August, having last played in 2015 for Fluminense.

He started Sunday's game and showed some bright touches, and he was involved in the opening goal.

The former Barcelona superstar held off a defender before playing the pass that came before the assist for Giulio Donati's drive from outside the box.

He had earlier set up a chance for Donati from a corner, with the defender having his header saved.

At half-time there was a media circus around Ronaldinho, with journalists surrounding him, and former Brazil and AC Milan team-mate Dida joined him on the pitch.

Ronaldinho was substituted at the break with the score at 1-0.

A temporary stand, named the R10 in reference to Ronaldinho and his familiar shirt number, was built for the sold-out fixture at the Stadio Bruno Benelli.

The game was streamed in several countries around the world.

Ronaldinho trained once with the team, on Saturday, before Sunday's debut.

A team graphic beforehand showed him on the left side, but he mostly played centrally.

In his peak playing years, Ronaldinho was one of the best players in the world - as well as one of the most popular for his joyful demeanour and exuberant skill.

He won the 2002 World Cup with Brazil, the 2006 Champions League with Barcelona, and league titles with Barca and AC Milan - plus the Ballon d'Or and Fifa World Player of the Year awards in 2005.

He also played for Paris St-Germain as well as Gremio, Flamengo, Atletico Mineiro and Fluminense in his homeland, plus Mexican side Queretaro.

Ronaldinho scored 299 goals in his regular career and had been hoping to have a chance for number 300 for Ravenna. He would have taken a penalty had they been awarded one.

"It was lovely to be here, playing, having the build-up in the dressing room," Ronaldinho told Sky Sport Italia.

And asked if he might play again for Ravenna, who are second in their Serie C group, he said: "If the president calls me, I'll be back."

All of Ravenna's players - and not just the starting XI - posed with Ronaldinho in the team photo before kick-off

#888. ‘We want to win it’: Tuchel says Nations League can set up England for Euro 2028 glory

Winning Nations League ‘the best preparation’ for Euros

England to be seeded in Friday’s draw after Spain win

Thomas Tuchel believes winning the Nations League would provide England with the springboard to Euro 2028 glory. The head coach watched his team close out the calendar year with a sensational 3-2 victory against Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium on ­Sunday.

It meant England leapfrogged the world champions to finish top of their Nations League group and ensured seeded status for the ­quarter-final draw on Friday. England will co‑host the European Championship and Tuchel wants to go into it as the Nations League winners.

“It is for me and for us,” he said when asked about the importance of the Nations League and its potential to help a team to bigger and better things. “I saw and heard about the celebrations in Portugal when they won it last year [beating Spain on penalties in the final]. It is just the best preparation we can have for the Euros. We don’t think so far, but it’s a fact.

“We want to have these matches on the highest level to prove ourselves, to gain in confidence and to see where we are … to adjust our game where we need a bit of adjustment. That’s what this Nations League is perfect for. We want to win it. But first of all, we need to win the quarter-final.”

The defender Ezri Konsa echoed Tuchel’s thoughts. “The Nations League is a trophy and silverware going into the Euros would be ­massive for us,” he said. “We want to win the Euros and we know it is on home soil. That will give us a ­massive boost.”

England surged into a 3-0 lead against Spain only to have Elliot Anderson sent off in the 63rd minute when he conceded a penalty. Mikel Oyarzabal scored it and the closing stages were nervy for England. There were shades of the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentinaas England sought desperately to defend their advantage.

“Playing with 10 men against the world champions would be difficult,” Konsa said. “The amount of balls coming into the box we dealt with really well.

“The World Cup has gone. We have passed that. We are focused on winning each game and we know we have the Euros coming up.

Max Dowman (pictured) became England Under-21s’ youngest-ever goalscorer by grabbing the late winner in a 3-2 friendly victory over France at Ashton Gate.

Carsley had handed a first start to promising Arsenal youngster Dowman and he proved to be the hero, tapping in from Harrison Armstrong's pass to give England the win at only 16 years old. Press Association

“It’s very important to end the year on a high. You end it with huge confidence going into next year’s set of games. We are taking it camp by camp. But going into March [and the Nations League quarter-finals] we will have a lot of confidence.”

#887. Gypsy Rose Blanchard's Partner Ken Urker’s Cause of Death Confirmed

Following the death of Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s partner Ken Urker, a coroner has confirmed he died from

More information has come to light about Ken Urker’s death.

A little more than one month after the 34-year-old—who shared daughter Aurora, 21 months, with Gypsy Rose Blanchard—was found dead in his Louisiana home on Oct. 1, Urker’s cause of death has been officially attributed to accidental poly substance drug toxicity, also known as an accidental drug overdose.

The Lafourche Parish Coroner’s Office confirmed the case is now complete, and no further testing is pending.

Prevously, the Sheriff's Office stated they found drug paraphernalia, including syringes and a spoon, in Urker's bathroom next to a "brown powdery substance" after his body was discovered in bed.

"Deputies located a syringe and a handgun on the nightstand next to the bed," read a police report obtained by E! News Oct. 2. "Mr. Urker was found lying on the bed on his back, cold to the touch, and appeared to have been there for an extended period of time."

Noting his face and arms were "blue," officers said Urker had "a paper towel placed on his left arm with what appeared to be blotches of blood."

The confirmation echoes what Blanchard previously said of her boyfriend’s passing, telling People he’d overdosed before passing away in his bed.

At the time, Blanchard, 35, grappled with whether or not Urker’s overdose had been intentional.

“He was not in a good state of mind lately,” she explained to the outlet on Oct. 1, adding that her partner had endured “an unimaginable level of public scrutiny and relentless cyberbullying across social media platforms.”

"The cruelty directed toward him was something no human being should have to endure,” the Life After Lockup star continued. “I believe the tremendous weight of that scrutiny and harassment had a profound impact on him, and I hope his passing serves as a reminder that there is a real person behind every screen, every headline, and every comment.”

Blanchard's family also noticed that Urker had been struggling before his death. Her half-brother Dylan Blanchard and his wife Anita Blanchard told police that Urker "made comments of being depressed and upset" while attending church with them the night before he died, according to the police report.

The couple went to "check on" him at home Oct. 1 when they discovered his body, with the sister-in-law telling police that Urker was "in a 'dark place' and he did not show up to work today," per the command log obtained by E! News. She also told authorities Urker had made threats to kill himself.

As Gypsy Rose Blanchard grapples with the loss of her partner, she’s dedicated to preserving Urker’s legacy and ensuring Aurora will always know who her father truly was.

But in the meantime, she was letting herself feel her grief.

“I’m in disbelief. I can’t think,” she admitted. “I’ve screamed until my throat burns.”

"He will forever be my soulmate and my red string, a connection that time, distance, and even death can never erase," she said. "Above all, Ken loved our daughter, Aurora. She is a beautiful reflection of his enduring spirit, and through her, a part of him will always remain with us."

For a look back at some of Urker and Blanchard’s sweetest moments together, read on.

Gypsy Rose Blanchard told E! News she knew Ken Urker was the one "probably the day I met him back in 2017."At the time, she was serving a 10-year prison sentence after pleading guilty to second-degree murder for her role in the 2015 killing of her mom Clauddine "Dee Dee" Blanchard.

The couple, who got engaged in 2018, even managed to create a festive atmosphere while Blanchard was incarcerated.

They split up in 2019 but, as Blanchard later noted, fate would come back to find them...

While Blanchard went on to tie the knot with teacher Ryan Anderson in 2022, she filed for divorce after less than two years of marriage. She and Urker Ken reunited in the spring of 2024.

"We are together and in a wonderful place in our relationship," she told TMZ that April. "We know it is going to be a long road ahead but are excited for the future."

Cloudy skies couldn't put a damper on the rekindled pair's mood.

Whatever he said had Blanchard beaming in a video about their "love story."

Blanchard shared a collage of some of her and Urker's most adorable moments a few weeks before revealing her pregnancy with their first child together.

At the time, she noted that their baby was due in January 2025.

The two found out they were expecting a baby girl during a sex reveal party in August 2024.

Before they become a family of three, Blanchard and Urker dined at a table for two during a September 2024 date night.

The parents-to-be took a trip to California, including Marina Del Rey, that October.

And while Blanchard noted on Instagram the view of San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge was "incredible," she added, "the company made it unforgettable."

The duo sported their shades in this sunny snap.

#886. ‘Inexcusable’ stadium sagas provide NWSL with unwelcome reality check

Problems faced by Gotham FC and Washington Spirit over staging of their playoff semi-finals shows the league still has work to do

In so many ways, Icahn Stadium, tucked away on Randall’s Island in the Harlem River, is a fantastic place to watch soccer.

The 5,000-seat facility was thrown together in the early 2000s, constructed to replace Downing Stadium, an aging relic that hosted Pelé’s first match with the New York Cosmos 51 years ago. It sits in the shadow of the Triborough Bridge and in the late afternoon fans get one of the more spectacular backdrops in American soccer: the silhouette of the Manhattan skyline framed against the warm orange and red hues of the sunset. The playing surface, replaced in 2024 by Major League Soccer’s NYC FC, is immaculate.

So, yes, the stadium has its charms. But it is no place to host an NWSL match, let alone one in the postseason.

Gotham FC were forced to host their semi-final against the Kansas City Current at Icahn on Sunday because the club deemed the pitch at their usual home – Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, New Jersey – to be unsafe. The playing surface was widely and deservedly derided after the club’s quarter-final win over Seattle last weekend, with players from both teams calling it “atrocious” and “so bad.” Reign coach Laura Harvey put it even more bluntly, saying that there is “no way a playoff game should be played on that shit.”

Just down I-95 in Washington DC, the Washington Spirit faced their own issues when hosting the other NWSL semi-final on Saturday. For a moment, it looked as if they’d have to play at cavernous Northwest Stadium, the home of the NFL’s Washington Commanders, an almost universally despised venue. The Spirit share Audi Field with MLS’s DC United, who are effectively their landlords; United had already arranged to host a Division III college football game there on Saturday – only last-minute bargaining allowed the Spirit to use the stadium.

The two matches – one at a stadium fit for lower-division soccer and the other played on a field with American football markings – painted a stark picture of where the NWSL, despite its explosive growth in recent years, stands in the pecking order of professional sports in the United States.

On Sunday it may have cost Gotham, who were defeated by the Current. Gotham were well-supported at Icahn, where a near-capacity, partisan crowd filled the venue with noise throughout the evening. But it only helped so much: for the second match in a row, Gotham did not register a single shot on goal.

Midfielder Midge Purce, whose second-half cross created the home side’s only goal of the evening – an own goal – was not in any hurry to peg the club’s performance on the venue switch, saying that such things are “never an excuse” for poor performances. Still, the situation felt undeniably consequential for a club who were nearly unplayable at home this year.

“I would say it’s inexcusable,” Purce said. “It’s not what you want in a professional league, for women who are progressing in the United States, we’re supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. We always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans and we earned that right throughout the season.”

Purce went on to absolve Gotham’s ownership of responsibility, saying they had done “absolutely everything they can do to make the best situation for us”. She added: “If I knew who to blame, I would ‘at’ them. I don’t have the names.”

Purce was not arguing, of course, that the game should have been played on an inferior playing surface at Sports Illustrated, and neither was her head coach, Juan Carlos Amorós, who said prioritizing player safety was the “right decision.” Still, the Spaniard lamented the move, speaking wistfully about how it may have affected the outcome.

“I think it is part of the sadness,” Amorós told the media. “I think we will never know what would have happened if we had played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch … It has been a sad weekend. I also think about the situation in Washington yesterday. You know this league deserves better. The two arguably best teams, most consistent, having to deal with these situations. And then yesterday, you know, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you’re seeing those American football lines ... we couldn’t play in our own ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games.”

The Current do not generally deal with this issue, as they are one of a handful of NWSL teams who own and operate their own stadium. The club’s head coach, Chris Armas, was quick to point out that he wasn’t entirely familiar with the intricacies of what led to Sunday’s game ending up at Icahn.

“There seemed to be some noise around it,” Armas said. “And rightfully so, but listen – it was a change for them and a change for us. Where the league is at, and how we’re coming along, our league is moving fast. Expansion, the quality of play, the players, the coaches. Things can’t be perfect yet. That stuff will come. Stadiums are going to come, facilities are going to be built. But everything has to catch up – and we’re not there. We can be critical for sure. But the future is bright for our league.”

Gotham won’t have to deal with playing their matches in New Jersey for much longer as they’ve long-planned to move into Etihad Park, NYC FC’s future home ground, in 2028. Yet even then they’ll be playing in a facility they don’t own. And while the future of the NWSL as a whole may look bright, this past weekend’s semi-finals offer a needed – yet unwelcome – reality check.

Travis Kelce is shaking off his latest injury.

#884. How did England cling on against Spain and what did Tuchel do differently?

James Trafford (right) kept Spain out in the latter stages

England held on to beat Spain 3-2 with a backs-to-the-wall finale in the Nations League to finish top of their group.

But many observers would have been feeling a sense of deja vu from the World Cup semi-final when England sat back and were beaten by Argentina.

So what was different this time? BBC Sport has a look.

First of all the context of the two games was entirely different.

England were 1-0 up against Argentina in the 55th minute on neutral territory in Atlanta - and still had all their players.

Anthony Gordon had put them ahead but Lionel Messi set up Enzo Fernandez and then Lautaro Martinez late on.

But against Spain the best performance of Thomas Tuchel's reign had them 3-0 up through goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

Elliot Anderson then fouled Lamine Yamal for a penalty, which Mikel Oyarzabal scored - and that began the siege at a partisan Riyadh Air Metropolitano.

Nico Williams made it 3-2 but Spain could not find an equaliser, thanks in part to England keeper James Trafford.

"Half an hour feels like two hours against a team like this [with 10 men]," Tuchel told ITV afterwards. "That's the way it is. Without the red card we were clear winners."

60 minutes of perfection, 30 minutes of chaos - an England win for the ages

England cling on to stun world champions Spain in thriller

Making defensive subs is fine when it works - but when it does not, boy will a manager hear about it.

In the World Cup last 16, England had been 2-1 up against Mexico in the Azteca when Jarell Quansah was sent off.

Tuchel brought on three defenders for a defender, a midfielder and a forward.

But England won 3-2 and Dan Burn's cameo was the stuff of legend.

However, nine days later with England 1-0 up against Argentina, Tuchel did the same again - three defenders on for a defender, midfielder and forward.

The first of those subs, with Konsa replacing Anthony Gordon, was in the 72nd minute.

And England just sat back until Argentina broke their resistance.

However, against Spain this time, despite England being down to 10 men and facing incessant pressure, Tuchel was not so quick with defensive subs.

Myles Lewis-Skelly, replacing Harry Kane, was the first on after 78 minutes - 15 minutes after Anderson's sending off. And then five minutes later he brought on two more players - but one of them was a striker in Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Burn replaced fellow defender White in the 89th minute.

"Harry played 78 minutes, Jude [Bellingham] 83 minutes and then just defending and defending, it's tiring," explained Tuchel.

"So we needed fresh energy. I was asked yesterday what happens if there needs to be a critical or crucial substitution. And I said, I feel free enough to take any substitution if I think it is necessary to help the team and to influence the game.

"I feel free enough to do that and I think there was a lot of defending needed. So we just went for some fresh legs."

Win over world champions Spain is a 'statement' - Tuchel

England actually faced more of a siege this time than against the Argentines, the stats confirm.

In the final 30 minutes they faced 19 shots from Spain, with seven on target and an expected goals (xG) total of 2.53.

Argentina, in that time, had 10 shots, with four on target and an xG of 1.41.

In terms of passes from England the numbers were similar with 65 against Argentina and 61 against Spain - both times with an accuracy rate of about 64%.

In Thursday's 2-1 win against Croatia, as a comparison, they tried 557 passes with accuracy of 89%.

"For half an hour it was Mexico reloaded and it felt like we were back in the Azteca. We had to overcome 30 minutes which, against Spain, felt like three hours," Tuchel told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"The difficult thing is it's not only a red card, it's a red card, and a goal so that makes a completely new game. Thirty minutes against the world champion feels like three hours. I said it before in the stadium and wave after wave after wave."

England were criticised for blowing a 2-1 half-time lead at Wembley in their first Nations League game with Spain.

But on that day their final 30-minute figurers were much better - with only five shots faced and 176 attempted passes with a 90% accuracy.

So what was different this time? Perhaps the team showed more resilience and unity?

After Spain had pulled one back England's players had a huddle.

"I love the fact the team went into a huddle and if anything the manager's stepped back because he wants to see the player reaction," said ex-England defender Matt Upson on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I almost think that the trauma from that sending off of Elliot Anderson has almost been a positive thing for England because it's given the team a chance to get together and cope in what is an incredibly difficult situation and come through the other side.

"There was so much going on in this game. England had to suffer and came through the other side."

Defender and goalscorer White was asked about the huddle after the game.

"Just stay calm, when you're one down it becomes more difficult and things change so it was all about managing that," he said.

Another factor was the performance of England keeper James Trafford, who made six saves - with four of them coming in the final 12 minutes of the game with the score at 3-2.

He made an incredible double save to deny Fermin Lopez and Lamine Yamal in injury time.

Upson said: "I think that double save was the moment for Spain and Trafford had the answers."

#883. 'I didn't know' - Price's controversial 145 checkout at Grand Slam explained

Gerwyn Price busts his score after hitting D20 - 10 over his required tally, but is given leg on account of having been given incorrect information by referee; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports up until the final on November 22

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Gerwyn Price produced a controversial 145 checkout en route to a routine Grand Slam of Darts victory over Sebastian Bialecki on Monday night in Wolverhampton.

Price, the three-time champion in Wolverhampton, came through 5-2 against Poland's Bialecki to book his place in the knockout stage.

However, there was controversy during the final Group E match as Price hit a 145 finish when he had 135 remaining in the fourth leg of the match.

'The Iceman' needed 135 to hold his throw, and he thought he had taken it out.

After hitting T19 he asked referee Charlie Corstophine what he had left and was told 88.

With 88 in mind, Price incorrectly hit T16 and D20 to finish off the leg and was given the hold.

Of course, Price believed he had gone the correct route for what he needed and went on to set up a last 16 date with Ryan Searle.

"I didn't know until I just walked in [to the press conference]," said Price. "I hit the first treble and I asked what I'd got left and he said 88.

"So I went treble 16 double top and he said game shot."

The Welshman admitted he was glad he didn't know or it would've weighed on his mind.

He added: "I know. I swear to God, I didn't even know until I came back here. I'm glad I didn't know because it probably would have played on my mind."

6.4.6 Errors in arithmetic shall stand as detailed on the scoreboard unless corrected prior to the next throw of the player whose score is in error. Any error in the score can be corrected by the Referee at any time until Game Shot is called inthat leg.

6.4.7 If the incorrect score resulted in a leg win the result will stand unless corrected prior to the start of the next leg.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Both players went into the contest with one win each after beating Joe Hunt, which made it a straight shoot-out with only the group winners reaching the knockout stage this year.

Price had opened his week with a 5-3 win over Hunt on Saturday, racing into a 4-0 lead before Hunt won three legs in a row. Bialecki needed a deciding leg to beat Hunt 5-4 on Sunday.

The new format has already seen Ross Smith, Jonny Clayton and Luke Woodhouse suffer shock exits and Price said: "I prefer the old one [format], obviously. I've had some good memories here. You can slip up once, but in this one you can't.

"As you can see, a couple of good boys have gone, and they probably thought they'd have a second chance. But once you lose a game, that's it; you're gone."

#882. Republic of Ireland captain Collins to miss Kosovo game

Collins picked up a knee injury in the closing stages against Austria on Saturday

Republic of Ireland captain Nathan Collins has been ruled out of Tuesday's must-win Nations League game against Kosovo with a knee injury.

Defender Collins picked up the issue in the closing stages of Saturday's 1-0 defeat by Austria in Linz and has returned to his club Brentford for treatment.

Queens Park Rangers' Jimmy Dunne will replace Collins - who also missed all four games of the September/October window - in the matchday squad for the Kosovo fixture.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has opted against drafting in Seamus Coleman, who is currently with the squad in a playing/coaching hybrid role.

"No, Jimmy Dunne will take Nathan's spot but we're really happy with what Seamus is giving to us," said Hallgrimsson.

"We obviously need to see the session today, that's the first session after the game, to see how players are but given everything I think we'll have the same squad including Jimmy."

Hallgrimsson rues 'painful' defeat for Republic of Ireland

The Republic of Ireland must win Tuesday's game to finish second in Group B3 and seal a place in March's promotion play-offs.

Hallgrimsson's side fell to a late 1-0 defeat by Kosovo in September before bouncing back to take four points from two matches against Israel.

"We need to get the same mentality, the same characters on the pitch against Kosovo," added Hallgrimsson.

"It is going to be as tough a game as it was in Austria, so just transfer that same attitude and if we do that, we will have a good byproduct, which is a win.

"It is clear we need to win the game, a draw will do nothing for us, and that is our mentality going into the game."

The Republic of Ireland's ultimate aim is securing a place at Euro 2028, which they will co-host alongside England, Wales and Scotland.

While goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher said playing in a tournament at home would be "amazing", he insisted the players are not looking that far ahead.

"Yeah, it would obviously be hard to describe, it would be an amazing experience, to play in a major tournament at home would be special," said the Brentford keeper.

"But I don't think we can think too far ahead into that. Obviously we've got to focus on tomorrow and trying to get a good result and we'll look towards that then when it comes.

"But we all know the opportunity that's there for us if we can perform, so it'll be a great opportunity."

#881. Grammy Nominations 2027 Snubs & Surprises: Noah Kahan, Raye & More

The Recording Academy revealed its 2027 Grammy nominations, with Beyoncé and Raye walking away with major recognition. Noah Kahan and Harry Styles, meanwhile, were absent in major categories.

Get ready to turn up the volume on the biggest night in music.

After all, the 2027 Grammy Awards nominations were announced on Nov. 16 with a pitch-perfect lineup of presenters, including David Guetta, Kehlani, Olivia Dean and Yungblud.

Taylor Swift proved she knows what it takes to put on a show, earning five nominations for her album The Life of a Showgirl as well as her Toy Story 5 track "I Knew It, I Knew You," including Album of the Year and Song of the Year.

Meanwhile, Olivia Rodrigo is ready for a golden evening after being nominated seven times over for her album you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love in categories including Album of the Year and Song of the Year, as well as Best Rock Performance and Best Rock Song for "What's Wrong With Me?" featuring Robert Smith.

Phoebe Bridgers made a triumphant return with her third solo album Lost Boys—her first in more than six years—earning seven nods like Album of the Year and Best Alternative Music Album.

Raye, for her part, was on every nomination shortlist, but she exceeded even the most elevated expectations, earning 11 nominations, tying Beyoncé's 2025 record for the most nominations by a single female artist in a single year.

That's not to say all the most-listened-to songs or albums made the list. Although fans expected Noah Kahan to be among the contenders for Album of the Year, The Great Divide appeared to fall flat with the Recording Academy, save for one nod for Best Contemporary Folk Album.

The same goes for Harry Styles, who failed to score a single nod for his album Kiss All The Time, Disco Occasionally. Meanwhile, despite Stella Lefty's massive hit "Boston" dominating charts this year, she failed to score a Best New Artist nomination.

And while Adéla prays every single night, she won't be sitting right at the Grammys for her earworm song "Nicole Kidman"—a decision she made for herself.

"I think it's a nomination you need to earn," she told Who What Wear earlier this month of the Song of the Year category. "I have so much more work to do before I even think of that. I have my tour, and I want to start writing my next album."

But that's not to say the 22-year-old won't return to try to prove her weight in gold.

"I think I need to do all the work I can this year and next in order to really earn it," she added. "Maybe in 2028, I'll feel like I truly deserve to be in that room."

As fans wait to see who wins big at the 2027 Grammy Awards on Feb. 7, keep reading for more snubs and surprises.

Abrams failed to snag any nominations for her latest album Daughter From Hell, which she submitted for Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album. Her single "Hit the Wall" was also absent from the Song of the Year, Record of the Year and Best Pop Solo Performance lists.

Abrams has previously received two nominations for Best New Artist in 2024 and Best Pop Duo Performance for "Us" which featured Taylor Swift in 2025.

While Grande picked up some surprise nominations for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance for "For Good" alongside Cynthia Erivo, as well as Song of the Year and Best Music Video for "hate that I made you love me," and Best Pop Vocal Album for Petal, she was snubbed for Album of the Year.

Although Kahan scored one nomination for Best Contemporary Folk Album, he was not included in the major categories like Album of the Year and Song of the Year for his hit The Great Divide.

Beyoncé is famously the most decorated Grammy-winning artist—the 35-time winner scored her 100th nomination this year— but her Best R&B Solo Performance nod for "Morning Dew (Donk)" was somewhat of a surprise considering its delayed release in celebration of B'Day's 20th anniversary in July.

This year was big for Hobert, who released her debut album Who's the Clown last year, but she failed to score a nod for Best New Artist. (Her brother Malcolm Todd was also left off the shortlist.)

That's actually not all for this much-anticipated sequel. The Devil Wears Prada 2 scored a surprise nomination for Best Compilation Soundtrack For Visual Media alongside Stranger Things season five, Wicked: For Good, The Wizard of Oz at the Sphere and Wuthering Heights.

It's been a long time coming for the first-time Grammy nominee, who scored her first nods for Best Dance/Electronic Recording for "Melatonin" as well as Best Dance Pop Recording for "Too Easy."

Swift wasn't totally snubbed by the Recording Academy—she earned nods for Record of the Year, Album of the Year, Song of the Year, Best Pop Duo Performance alongside Sabrina Carpenter, Best Song Written for a Visual Media and more. But The Life of a Showgirl was not among Best Pop Vocal Album contenders, while "I Knew It, I Knew You" was snubbed for Best Country Song and Best Country Solo Performance.

Still, it was a surprise to see "I Knew It, I Knew You" score a nomination for Song of the Year, a category introduced by Swift herself during the nomination livestream, given Swift's other hits from The Life of a Showgirl.

The hype hasn't died down, Wicked is still oh so very popular. Wicked: For Good scored two nominations including Best Song Written For Visual Media and Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance.

Disco All The Time, Grammy Occasionally. The "Aperture" singer failed to score recognition for his latest album in any category. Styles has three Grammy wins under his belt, including Album of the Year for Harry's House in 2023.

Her comeback is far from over. The pop star received her first Grammy nominations in 16 years, racking up nods for Best Dance Pop Recording, Best Dance/Electronic Recording, Best Dance/Electronic Album and Best Pop Duo/Group Performance for "Bring Your Love" alongside Carpenter.

Although Lefty rose to massive acclaim this year for hits like "Boston," she failed to receive any recognition by The Recording Academy.

Following a two-year hiatus, West scored a nod for Best Rap Album for Bully.

#879. What's at the top of Frick's Aberdeen to-do list?

Swiss club Luzern did not renew Mario Frick's contract this summer

Mario Frick arrives at Aberdeen with the Pittodrie side sitting second bottom of the table and a game against relegation rivals Kilmarnock first up.

Lose that match and they fall to the foot of the Scottish Premiership. No pressure.

Apart from the obvious, what is it that the new head coach has to do to restore Aberdeen to previous glory days and avoid becoming yet another managerial failure at Pittodrie?

Okay, maybe this was obvious. But it's Aberdeen's clearest weakness this season.

They have the joint worst attacking record in the league, having only scored 12 goals and routinely looked completely short of confidence in front of goal.

Kevin Nisbet, the club captain, has 14 goals for the season. Nine of those came in the run to the Premier Sports Cup semi-final. Behind him, no-one has more than two.

Most concerning of all is that the Dons' have created the lowest xG (15.3) in the league so far. Not only are they not creating very many quality chances, they're struggling to take them.

They have just 3.3 shots on target per match, with a shot conversion rate of just 7.3%. Both metrics are the worst in the league.

Only Falkirk have created fewer big chances (19 to Aberdeen's 22) - the difference being John McGlynn's side score them.

Getting the best out of Connor Ronan could be key for Mario Frick

One of the most frequent accusations that came predecessor Stephen Robinson's way was that his team lacked an identity and players looked unsure as to the tactical plan they had been told to carry out.

Given the Northern Irishman's clear style of play with St Mirren, that was a surprise.

His team in Paisley were known for their physically-domineering displays that were full of grit and graft. That wasn't the case in the North East.

Frick seemingly prefers a 4-4-2 formation, with the midfield playing in a diamond.

That might be bad news for new signings Tony Yogane and Lewis Smith, wingers who did get a look in under Robinson but struggled to make much of an impact.

Sticking to a consistent midfield will help with that. While Robinson regularly relied on Afeez Aremu in the middle of the park, the head coach often chopped and changed his midfield partner.

Of all of Aberdeen's 15 summer signings, Connor Ronan was the one that probably caused the most optimism. Another former St Mirren man, he impressed in his time in Paisley.

The Irishman won a move to Major League Soccer with Colorado Rapids off the back of that form and was also called up to the Republic of Ireland squad without winning a cap.

Eight goals from midfield in the 2021-22 season was a good return - and a couple of them were screamers.

Former Aberdeen midfielder Jamie McGrath recently reminded his old fanbase that they could do with replacing him after he scored a rocket for Hibs in the 4-0 win that did for Robinson.

Ronan could be the answer, playing in a similar role with the same attacking capabilities.

He has yet to hit the heights at Pittodrie, but if Frick can make him tick, the 28-year-old could fire Aberdeen back up the league table.

Stability & no slacking - what to expect from new Dons boss Frick

#878. Secrets of the vampires: genomes reveal how these bats live off blood alone

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Max Kozlov is a senior reporter with Nature in Washington DC.

All the better to eat you with: vampire bats (such as this common vampire bat, Desmodus rotundus) have an array of genetic adaptations that allow them to subsist on blood.Credit: Joel Sartore/Photo Ark/Nature Picture Library

A foraging vampire bat slices into sleeping prey and laps up about half of its own body weight in blood, causing its belly to balloon. Now, an analysis of the bats’ genomes and organs offers clues to how they stomach this gory diet.

The study1, posted on the preprint server bioRxiv on 7 November before being peer reviewed, provides a “high-resolution look into what it takes to build a vampire bat”, says Jasmin Camacho, an evolutionary developmental biologist at the Stowers Institute for Medical Research in Kansas City, Missouri, who was not involved in the research. “It’s one of the first times we can really see what those molecular signatures of being a blood specialist look like.”

Blood is a challenging meal: it contains mostly water, little sugar and fat, and toxic amounts of iron. Yet all three species of vampire bat survive exclusively on blood after reaching adulthood.

To understand how they pull this off, Michael Hiller, an evolutionary genomicist at the Senckenberg Research Institute in Frankfurt, Germany, and his colleagues generated genomes for all three vampire-bat species (Desmodus rotundus, Diaemus youngii and Diphylla ecaudata)and three other species of bat. They then compared the genomes. They also analysed gene activity in six organs for two of the vampire species and four species of non-vampiric bats.

The stomach stood out. In most mammals, the stomach bathes food in acid to aid digestion. In vampire bats, however, the researchers found that the organ has been repurposed into a stretchy, pH-neutral storage sac lined with thick layers of connective tissue that help it to expand after a feast.

Vampire bats’ stomachs can expand enormously to accommodate their meals of blood. Credit: Jon Flanders

To shed excess water quickly so that the bats can fly home, their stomachs ramp up activity of a fluid-transporting gene that is typically active in salivary and sweat glands by more than 900-fold, the analysis found. The function of these vampire-bat stomachs has changed so much from those of other mammals that the organs perhaps “deserve a different name”, Hiller says.

Despite the lack of fat in blood, the bats still retain some genes for digesting lipids. The activity of these genes is dialled down in adulthood but might enable nursing pups to digest their mother’s fat-rich milk before switching to blood after weaning, says Ken Welch Jr, a comparative physiologist at the University of Toronto in Canada. But the bats have lost some genes altogether, such as ones known to help animals to distinguish between sweet and bitter tastes2.

Using mosquitoes to vaccinate bats could curb the spread of deadly diseases

#877. Vinicius says transfer interest affected Real form

Vinicius Jr signed a new six-year contract with Real Madrid in August

Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr says he felt "truly overwhelmed" by transfer speculation in the summer, which has contributed to his mixed form at the start of the season.

The Brazil international has scored just once and provided three assists in 12 appearances for Jose Mourinho's side this season.

He was linked with a move to Premier League champions Arsenal this summer as he entered the final year of his contract, before signing an extension at Real.

The 26-year-old also says he did not train as much as he should have following Brazil's last-16 exit at the World Cup.

"I don't think I prepared as well as I could have after the World Cup, because the impact of that tournament is so significant for all Brazilians," he said.

"Being knocked out so early was something we hadn't expected. So, I took advantage of my holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in previous years.

"That may have affected my start to the season.

"On top of that, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs showing interest last summer, I felt truly overwhelmed, as with the situation at Real Madrid. But it's a very long season."

Vinicius received a red card for violent conduct in October when he pulled the hair of Villarreal midfielder Nathan Saliba, which led to a four-match suspension.

In his absence, record signing Yan Diomande has made the most of his opportunity on the left wing, scoring four goals.

Vinicius joined Real from Brazilian side Flamengo in 2018 and has scored more than 20 club goals in each of his past five seasons.

Mourinho's side are second in La Liga, three points behind rivals Barcelona, and return to league action when they host Celta Vigo on Saturday.

#874. Next James Bond Revealed After Years-Long Search: See His First Teaser

More than five years after Daniel Craig's martini was shaken, not stirred, Robert Pattinson will officially take on the role of James Bond in the upcoming film.

The latest James Bond update is shocking. Positively shocking.

After years of speculation as to who would be holstering the Walther PPK and asking for his martini shaken, not stirred, Robert Pattinson is grabbing the keys to the Aston Martin as the titular secret agent.

Several leading men have vied for the role, with Daniel Craig last pouring himself a glass of Macallan in 2021's No Time to Die. In fact, Jack Lowden—whose Slow Horses costar Gary Oldman publicly threw his support behind—Callum Turner, Jacob Elordi, Henry Cavill and Damson Idris were just a few names that sparked casting rumors

Although the actors' involvement was simply speculation over the years, former Bond Pierce Brosnan—who headlined GoldenEye, Tomorrow Never Dies, The World Is Not Enough and Die Another Day between 1995 and 2002—believes Aaron Taylor-Johnson could keep the British end up.

"I think he would be very good," he reflected in an April 2025 interview with Yahoo! Entertainment, adding that they costarred in a 2009 film that he also executive produced. "I cast him in one of the movies I made a long time ago called The Greatest, actually, and he played the Greatest."

"This young man came on the set," Brosnan recalled of the then-18-year-old actor, "and took the space, filled the space with passion and energy. So yeah, I think if he wished it, wanted it and got it, he would be great."

For Taylor-Johnson's part, however, he doesn't have an inflated opinion of himself when it comes to the possibility of the prestigious honor.

"It's not really for me to say anything," the now-36-year-old told Esquire in August 2023. "I just focus on the things I can have my hands in right now. What's in front of me right now."

Identity Confirmed pic.twitter.com/FCU5A9c1wk

Although several celebs have been fancast as the 007 agent, the opportunity is quite daunting. For instance, Theo James isn't sure if he's up for the pressure.

"Everyone's interested in that because it's a big part of British cultural identity, but that probably wouldn't be me," he admitted to The Guardian in March 2024. "I do think there are better people for that job. And, honestly, it would be terrifying: if you do that, there's no going back."

Meanwhile, Glen Powell was adamant that anyone but him should take on the role since he's more suited for a cowboy hat than a tux.

"I'm a Texan," he told The Hollywood Reporter in August. "My family and I joke around, I can play Jimmy Bond, but I should not be playing James Bond. Get an authentic Brit for that job. That's who belongs in that tuxedo."

#873. Cameroon, Senegal and Benin close in on Afcon 2027 qualification

Nicolas Jackson has 12 goals in 18 appearances for Aston Villa and Senegal this season

Nicolas Jackson was on target again as Senegal, Cameroon and Benin moved to the brink of qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) with away victories.

After Aston Villa striker Jackson had opened the scoring, Senegal gave up a 2-0 lead against Sudan before two late goals sealed a 4-2 win, while five-time Afcon winners Cameroon cruised to a 3-0 triumph over Namibia.

A goal in second-half stoppage time from Ede Oloko sealed a 1-0 success for Benin against Central African Republic.

All three sides are on 10 points in their respective groups after four rounds of matches and will progress to next year's finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda if other results go their way on Tuesday.

Elsewhere, Jordan Ayew's first-half penalty was enough for Ghana to register back-to-back victories over Somalia in Group C.

The Black Stars had home advantage for what should have been an away tie, with the game played in Sekondi-Takoradi because the Ocean Stars do not have a stadium fit for international football.

Ayew had a penalty saved as Ghana beat Somalia 2-0 in the reverse fixture last Thursday, but the Sheffield United forward kept his composure when he sent the goalkeeper the wrong way in the 36th minute after Brandon Thomas-Asante had been pulled down in the box.

Ghana, who parted company with Carlos Queiroz after losing their opening two fixtures, move level in the table with The Gambia, with both sides on six points.

Salah scores twice as Egypt and Nigeria win Afcon 2027 qualifiers

Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

The Gambians are themselves three points adrift of group leaders Ivory Coast before they host the Elephants on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, Guinea moved to the top of Group D after Yakhouba Barry scored twice in their 3-1 away win over Eritrea in neutral Cairo.

The West Africans lead South Africa, who travel to Kenya on Tuesday, by two points in a group with only one qualification spot available because the Kenyans are assured of a spot at the finals as co-hosts.

And Zimbabwe beat Equatorial Guinea 3-0 in Harare to go two points behind Group E table toppers DR Congo.

Thando Ngwenya, Tawanda Chirewa and Tawanda Maswanhise were all on target for the Warriors before Equatorial Guinea's Josete Miranda had a penalty saved and Saul Coco was sent off for the visitors late on.

The National Thunder were without first choice goalkeeper Jesus Owono after he asked not to be selected following his involvement in a collision with Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who died the day after the incident.

DR Congo, Ivory Coast, Mali and Morocco can all book their tickets to the tournament when the fourth round of fixtures culminates with 18 matches on Tuesday.

The final two rounds of qualifiers will be held in March next year, with Afcon 2027 scheduled to be held in East Africa from 19 June to 17 July.

Patrick Vieira's Senegal survived a scare in neutral Juba after Jackson's early goal put the Teranga Lions ahead and a low strike from Brentford left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf made it 2-0 midway through the first half.

Sudan hit back through Al-Gozoli Nooh and Salah Adel to level proceedings with 15 minutes to play, but Pathe Mboup's lob made it 3-2 in the 87th minute and Paul Mendy made the points safe for the West Africans in the first minute of added time.

Senegal are still awaiting the outcome of their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport over the destination of the 2025 Afcon title.

The Teranga Lions beat Morocco 1-0 after extra time in January's final, but a Confederation of African Football appeals board stripped them of the title two months later, decreeing Senegal had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them.

Mahamadou Nagida opened the scoring for Cameroon against Namibia in neutral Botswana with a stunning volley from outside the box in the 12th minute, and Ryan Fosso's deflected effort doubled the lead just before the hour mark.

Saidou Alioum made it 3-0 with a fine first-time volley with 19 minutes remaining, and David Pagou's men will be assured of a place at Afcon 2027 if Congo-Brazzaville fail to beat Comoros on Tuesday.

Central African Republic 0-1 Benin (Group F)

#870. 60 minutes of perfection, 30 minutes of chaos - an England win for the ages

Harry Kane scored for a record-equalling seventh England away game

Thomas Tuchel went with bold words when reminded about the caution that sabotaged England's World Cup hopes and left them with so much to prove against Spain in the Nations League on Sunday.

In a media theatre at the Metropolitano in Madrid, head coach Tuchel's sixth sense led him to go public with what he was convinced England would produce against the world champions.

Tuchel looked his inquisitors in the eyes and declared: "We are up for something spectacular."

To say Tuchel and England kept their word was a masterpiece of understatement after the finest night of the head coach's reign resulted in a 3-2 victory that was large parts magnificent, some parts madness - and all parts spectacular.

It also ended Spain's 43-game unbeaten run - setting aside their penalty shootout defeat by Portugal in the 2025 Nations League final.

If England and Tuchel could be accused of being cowed by pressure when they led Argentina in the ill-fated World Cup semi-final, they were thrillingly positive in this unforgiving Madrid environment.

The question being asked when England held a one-goal advantage through Harry Kane's penalty at half-time was 'what would theirs and Tuchel's reaction be?' Stick or twist?

Would Tuchel tell England to press their foot on the pedal for acceleration? Or would he take the approach of going into reverse gear, as he did to ill-fated effect against Argentina?

How did England cling on against Spain and what did Tuchel do differently?

Who swaggered around like he owned the place? Spain v England ratings

England hold on to stun world champions Spain in thriller

The answer was delivered when they added goals from Arsenal duo Ezri Konsa and Ben White in the first 12 minutes of the second half.

This being England, they then created a mess for themselves when Elliot Anderson was sent off for fouling Lamine Yamal in the area after 65 minutes, although the main culprit was Jarell Quansah for initially conceding possession.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the spot and, when Yamal set up Nico Williams for Spain's second with 15 minutes left, it looked like more than an hour of faultless England football might be wasted.

But not a bit of it, as goalkeeper James Trafford produced heroics and England defended with every fibre to close out this landmark win.

Was this the statement victory that was almost demanded of Tuchel as recompense for the World Cup disappointment, a performance to convince the doubters?

"We're fully aware what we put out there," said Tuchel afterwards. "What a performance we put out for 65 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up.

"Of course, the red card and the penalty changed the momentum and the characteristics of the game... but we know, and the players know very, very well, what they put out there. That is the statement - and that is the significance of this victory."

Simple details of the game barely touch the sides of a night filled with quality and glorious chaos, vindication for Tuchel and England's positive approach.

Spain opened with an ostentatious parade of the World Cup in front of England's players as the teams lined up, perhaps a psychological reminder of the superiority that has seen them dominate international football.

What followed, at times literally, reduced Spain's supporters to stunned silence and their players to a shell-shocked shambles chasing the shadows that were overpowering them.

England's white shirts were everywhere but Spain could not get near them. The tormentors had become the tormented.

It was alien territory for a Spain side that has carried all before them, while England's fans tucked away high in a corner of this vast arena were equally unbelieving as a dream unfolded in front of them.

England, for 65 minutes, were in a different class to Spain. And, yes, you have read that right.

From the first whistle, employing a suffocatingly high press, England ran all over Spain.

When White crowned a superb move with the third goal four minutes after Konsa's second, it looked, remarkably, to be a case of how big England's victory margin would be.

In the end, the margin was narrow but the stature and significance of England's victory was huge.

Tuchel labelled this meeting with Spain as "proof of concept at the highest level".

There was no doubt the German manager and England were under fierce scrutiny after the manner of the collapse, mentally and tactically, against Argentina at the World Cup.

Here they delivered the proof they can match the best then beat them.

Win over world champions Spain is a 'statement' - Tuchel

If the vital signs were being forensically examined for evidence Tuchel has learned lessons from a chastening World Cup, that England have improved after that harrowing experience, this game delivered these conclusions.

Of course, England must do it again. Do it when the pressure and expectation in at its highest.

The Nations League is competitive but cannot be compared to a World Cup and European Championship, both titles currently in the possession of the team they beat here.

But England's world-class players delivered - Kane inevitably with his 93rd international goal, but Jude Bellingham was on a level of his own, the outstanding performer on both sides with an individual display simply confirming he is the player with everything.

And Tuchel got his big calls right, especially selecting Trafford, who responded superbly in a frantic closing phase. White, making a strong claim for the right-back berth, not only scored a goal but produced crucial challenges in the face of relentless, albeit belated, Spain pressure.

"This was the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness," said Tuchel. "It was on the highest level football wise in all aspects of the game. We did everything that needs to be done together.

"The deep build-up. The high press. The counter-attack. The tracking. The defensive phases. This was an excellent performance and of course a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

"We overcame some difficult moments in the end. That's how it is. But we are very well aware which steps we took now through after the World Cup."

England's win means they top their Nations League group, but the importance spreads much wider than simply a league table.

The first 65 minutes were simply breathtaking. Spain wilting under attack after attack. Spain rattled until they shook as England refused to allow them meaningful possession.

After Anderson's dismissal, bad memories were revisited as England were forced into a rearguard action, but any other result than the one that was eventually delivered would have been a huge injustice.

England survived 29 nervous minutes, including added time, to make a powerful statement about their current status, which is much healthier than when recriminations about Tuchel's approach provided the post-World Cup narrative.

"I'm very impressed with the steps that we took after the World Cup", said Tuchel. "We wanted to get better, better in a deep build-up, get better in defending in a low block and, on top of it, we wanted always to impose our identity and the way we want to play against every opponent.

"I think this was clearly visible throughout the whole group phase. The results followed with an excellent group phase."

Was this the finest performance of Tuchel's time in charge? Most observers felt so, but the head coach was best placed to answer.

"Yes, given the circumstances," he said, "and the pressure, the quality, where we played in this building against the reigning world champions, unbeaten in 43 matches. Putting a performance out there in Madrid, and in this environment, was a very complete performance."

Tuchel will, of course, need repeat performances - but the outstanding ability and character England displayed here to beat the World Cup holders will deliver a huge injection of confidence and self-belief.

#869. Taylor Swift Makes Surprise Appearance During Grammy Nominations

Taylor Swift made a surprise feature during the 2027 Grammy nomination ceremony, poking fun at herself before Album and Song of the Year were announced: “I'm zero for eight.”

Through the daze of the Grammy nominations, Taylor Swift came back when it mattered.

The 14-time Grammy winner made a surprise appearance during the nomination ceremony on Nov. 16, making sure the announcement of the final two categories hit just the perfect note.

“Good morning America, it's Taylor,” Swift said as she appeared on screen dressed in a simple back long sleeve shirt and necklaces. “I'm very honored that the Grammys have asked me to be here to help reveal the last two categories for the Grammy nominations.”

“I first wanted to start off by saying congratulations to anyone who's nominated for a Grammy this year in any category,” she continued, “because what this means is that your peers, your fellow musicians, producers, engineers, artists, writers, they love what you made, and that's the coolest feeling in the world. I hope you have a really wonderful day.”

She then revealed the last two categories of the ceremony were to be Album of the Year and Song of the Year—two categories, as she joked, she’s quite familiar with.

"The last two categories to be announced—one of them I've had a lot of luck in,” the 36-year-old said, before quipping. “The other one I'm zero for eight.”

After all, she has been nominated for Album of the Year seven times—earning her eighth just seconds after her onscreen appearance for The Life of a Showgirl—and has won the category a record four times.

As for Song of the Year, the Midnights artist has indeed been nominated eight times but has yet to bring home the Grammy. Maybe the ninth time will prove the charm, having been nominated for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” the song she wrote for Toy Story 5.

She’s facing some stiff competition, however. Also nominated in the category are “Berghain” by Rosalía, Björk and Yves Tumor, “Choosin’ Texas” by Ella Langley, “The Cure” by Olivia Rodrigo, “Hate That I Made You Love Me” by Ariana Grande, “Man I Need” by Olivia Dean, “Risk It All” by Bruno Mars and “Where Is My Husband!” by Raye, who earned the most nominees of any artist with 11.

The Album of the Year battle will be easily as fraught, with powerhouses such as Phoebe Bridgers’ first album in six years, Lost Weekend, Dean’s The Art of Loving, Langley’s Dandelion, Mars’ The Romantic, Raye’s This Music May Contain Hope, Rodrigo’s You Seem Pretty Sad For a Girl So In Love and Rosalía’s Lux.

But while some of these noms may have seemed assured, at every award show there are nominations that come as surprises and the notable absences that come as a shock. Read on for a look at this year’s Grammys snubs and surprises.

Abrams failed to snag any nominations for her latest album Daughter From Hell, which she submitted for Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album. Her single "Hit the Wall" was also absent from the Song of the Year, Record of the Year and Best Pop Solo Performance lists.

Abrams has previously received two nominations for Best New Artist in 2024 and Best Pop Duo Performance for "Us" which featured Taylor Swift in 2025.

While Grande picked up some surprise nominations for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance for "For Good" alongside Cynthia Erivo, as well as Song of the Year and Best Music Video for "hate that I made you love me," and Best Pop Vocal Album for Petal, she was snubbed for Album of the Year.

Although Kahan scored one nomination for Best Contemporary Folk Album, he was not included in the major categories like Album of the Year and Song of the Year for his hit The Great Divide.

Beyoncé is famously the most decorated Grammy-winning artist—the 35-time winner scored her 100th nomination this year— but her Best R&B Solo Performance nod for "Morning Dew (Donk)" was somewhat of a surprise considering its delayed release in celebration of B'Day's 20th anniversary in July.

This year was big for Hobert, who released her debut album Who's the Clown last year, but she failed to score a nod for Best New Artist. (Her brother Malcolm Todd was also left off the shortlist.)

That's actually not all for this much-anticipated sequel. The Devil Wears Prada 2 scored a surprise nomination for Best Compilation Soundtrack For Visual Media alongside Stranger Things season five, Wicked: For Good, The Wizard of Oz at the Sphere and Wuthering Heights.

It's been a long time coming for the first-time Grammy nominee, who scored her first nods for Best Dance/Electronic Recording for "Melatonin" as well as Best Dance Pop Recording for "Too Easy."

Swift wasn't totally snubbed by the Recording Academy—she earned nods for Record of the Year, Album of the Year, Song of the Year, Best Pop Duo Performance alongside Sabrina Carpenter, Best Song Written for a Visual Media and more. But The Life of a Showgirl was not among Best Pop Vocal Album contenders, while "I Knew It, I Knew You" was snubbed for Best Country Song and Best Country Solo Performance.

Still, it was a surprise to see "I Knew It, I Knew You" score a nomination for Song of the Year, a category introduced by Swift herself during the nomination livestream, given Swift's other hits from The Life of a Showgirl.

The hype hasn't died down, Wicked is still oh so very popular. Wicked: For Good scored two nominations including Best Song Written For Visual Media and Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance.

Disco All The Time, Grammy Occasionally. The "Aperture" singer failed to score recognition for his latest album in any category. Styles has three Grammy wins under his belt, including Album of the Year for Harry's House in 2023.

Her comeback is far from over. The pop star received her first Grammy nominations in 16 years, racking up nods for Best Dance Pop Recording, Best Dance/Electronic Recording, Best Dance/Electronic Album and Best Pop Duo/Group Performance for "Bring Your Love" alongside Carpenter.

Although Lefty rose to massive acclaim this year for hits like "Boston," she failed to receive any recognition by The Recording Academy.

Following a two-year hiatus, West scored a nod for Best Rap Album for Bully.
