#816. Jane Lynch Reveals Whether She’ll Return for Glee Reboot

Jane Lynch shared her thoughts on the upcoming Glee reboot, revealing if she'd step back into Coach Sue Sylvester's tracksuit again.

Sue Sylvester may be picking up the whistle once again.

Glee fans have been curious about whether Jane Lynch will reprise her role as the cheerleading coach on the musical series' upcoming reboot, and she's now finally weighing in.

"If I am asked to partake, the answer will be yes," she said on the Nov. 16 episode of The Jennifer Hudson Show. "I would love to do Sue Sylvester for the rest of my life."

The 66-year-old went on to share what it would feel like to play the iconic villain again over a decade after Glee originally came to an end in 2015.

"You know, I wonder though how far we can take her now, because if you look out in the world, there are a lot of Sue Sylvesters out there,” Lynch mused. “I think I kind of made the mold for everybody, but I can’t wait. I think it would be really, really fun to do it again and to get to wear tracksuits every day. And my that was my most favorite wardrobe."

Though it remains to be seen which of the cast—which also included Matthew Morrison, Harry Shum Jr., Lea Michele, Chris Colfer, Amber Riley and more—will appear in the reboot, creator Ryan Murphy previously hinted that some William McKinley High School alums will be returning.

"I've been in touch with around 10 of the original cast members," he told Entertainment Tonight in September. "It's very sweet, and they all had a lot of questions, but they all were very enthusiastic about the idea."

Michele had also expressed interest in playing Rachel Berry again in a potential Glee revival—if it felt right.

"I love Glee," she told E! News in September. "I will always love Glee. I love Ryan Murphy. It just holds such a special place in my heart for me. So, I will follow Ryan wherever he goes."

In the meantime, keep reading for an encore on everything Glee...

A few years after Glee ended, Ryan Murphy reflected on the pop culture phenomenon and revealed how chaotic things were behind the scenes.

"It was the best time in my life and the worst time in my life," he told Entertainment Weekly, going on to admit, "There was a lot of infighting. There was a lot of people sleeping together and breaking up. It was good training for being a parent, I'll tell you that much."

He also reflected on his time on the show, looking back with some regret on how he handled things as the showrunner.

"I was there with them all day long, and then we'd finish work and we'd go out and have fun all night, and I guess in a weird, twisted way, I was trying to relive the childhood I never had," he told THR. "I thought they wanted a parent, and they didn't. They didn't want me to tell them what to f—king do. They didn't want me to tell them how to treat each other or what the world was like at the end of the day. I wish I could go back and do that differently with a lot of those actors. Some of them I'm still very close to: Lea Michele, Chord Overstreet, Darren Criss — but there were some that didn't work out well, and I regret that. I guess I just wish I had been able to let them figure it out for themselves."

Going on to create Scream Queens, American Horror Story, Pose and other hit series, Murphy said Glee "was a great lesson in what not to do moving forward."

Fun fact: Ryan Murphy wrote the role of Rachel Berry with Lea Michele, a Broadway standout thanks to Spring Awakening, in mind. But not every cast member's journey to becoming a Gleek was so easy.

Before he was cast as Blaine, Criss auditioned for the role of Finn, the lead quarterback.

"It was the first audition I ever had. I auditioned for the pilot," he revealed at the Paleyfest panel. "And then I remember watching the pilot to see who got the part [I went out for] and seeing Cory [Monteith got it] and thinking, oh, obviously, right."

Another star who also auditioned for a different part was Colfer, who read for Artie originally. Producers were so impressed by the teen that they created the role of Kurt specifically for him.

In fact, Murphy revealed Colfer's audition was the inspiration behind creating The Glee Project, the show's reality competitions series that gave aspiring actors the chance to be cast on Glee.

"It's such a huge honor and I mean that's really special because I feel like if I inspired something that is giving kids a platform that is incredible," Colfer said.

The final cast member to join the show? Dianna Agron, who played head cheerleader Quinn Fabray, landing the role the day before they filmed the pilot.

Initially, Quinn was supposed to be the stereotypical mean girl, but Agron's nature ended up changing the role for the writers.

"When we cast Dianna as Quinn, she ruined the part for me," Murphy told Rolling Stone. "She was supposed to be the Cybill Shepherd, Last Picture Show c—, so to speak, but she humanized it. She can cry at the drop of a hat. So now her character has a conscience, a soul and great vulnerability."

Agron would leave the show after season three, returning only for the 100th episode.

Just like in the hallways of McKinley High, the Glee set featured a lot of flirtation and relationships between its young stars. (And even before the show, as Lea Michele revealed in her 2014 memoir Brunette Ambition that she and Matthew Morrison "actually dated back in for the day for a Broadway beat.")

Michele and Cory Monteith, whose characters were one of the show's most iconic couples," dated for several years before Monteith's tragic death in 2013, while Blake Jenner and Melissa Benoist, who now stars on Supergirl, married in 2015 after meeting on the set in 2012 when they also played love interests; they split in 2016 and their divorce was finalized the following year.

Naya Rivera and Mark Salling briefly dated in the show's earlier days and it wasn't an amicable split, as Rivera would write in her 2016 memoir, "I think everyone should have that one relationship where you look back and ask yourself, 'What the hell was I thinking?' You'll learn something and you won't regret it. Unless, of course, that relationship was with someone who had a sizable stash of child porn on his computer. Then, by all means, regret everything." Rivera was referring to Salling's child pornography indictment in 2017. In January 2018, Salling committed suicide at the age of 35.

While they first met when she guest-starred on Glee, Gwyneth Paltrow didn't begin dating future husband Brad Falchuk, one of Glee's co-creators, until she returned to the show in 2014, over a year after her split from Coldplay frontman Chris Martin.

"When you're going through a divorce and you think about going out with somebody, it's a weird thing," she told Howard Stern of taking it slowly with Falchuk, a recently-divorced father of two. "So I don't think it's the same as being 23 and running into someone at a coffee shop. It's just different. You have kids, you have divorce—it's just a lot of stuff."

While there were whispers of a romance between Kevin McHale (Artie) and Jenna Ushkowitz (Tina) during the show's run, it turns out they were just in a showmance, which became the new of their hit podcast.

Given its popularity and millions of downloads (including huge bumps for the original versions of the songs covered by the cast), you would think any band or artist would give Glee the rights to their songs. But there were several major bands that wouldn't let the glee club put their take on their tunes: Kings of Leon, with Murphy calling the band members "self-centered assholes" because they "missed the big picture" aka how the show could inspire kids to join arts education through their songs, namely their hit "Use Somebody." A mini-Twitter feud followed.

Guns N' Roses guitarist Slash also rejected Glee's request, saying he wasn't a fan of the show. "Usually I find people who make those comments, their careers are over' they're uneducated and stupid," Murphy said.

The Foo Fighters didn't approve the show's request either, with Dave Grohl calling out Murphy in an interview with THR.

"You shouldn't have to do f--king Glee," he said. "And then the guy who created Glee is so offended that we're not, like, begging to be on his f--king show...I watched 10 minutes...it's not my thing."

Colfer and Ushkowitz lived together during the show's run and often had cast parties at their apartment.

"Those of us who were obviously over-age would drink themselves into the oblivion," McHale said on Showmance, his podcast with Ushkowitz, before Colfer chimed in, "Oh, I drank too." (During a 2013 Paleyfest panel, Colfer revealed he actually had his first drink at their apartment.)

Amber Riley (Mercedes) smoked her first and last cigarette during one of their many late nights there, with the foursome being so close they called themselves JACK (the first initial of all of their names).

They also reminisced on their wild nights out while on their concert tour, with Riley revealing she got into a fight with a random girl while in London with the cast. After realizing she had punched the girl, she told their security team who then paid the girl off to stay quiet. Colfer, still not 21 at the time, admitted to sneaking into a lot of bars.

Because they were a young, close-knit cast, many things the stars were going through ended up on-screen, especially early on.

"There have been a couple of times when I have gone to Ryan Murphy and told him a couple of things that have happened to me, and then he writes it into the show," Colfer said in an interview with PR.com. "Or he'll ask me what song I would want to sing, in this situation or in that situation. I don't think any of us directly try to give input on the character or on the storyline, but they definitely steal things from us. I remember I was talking to Ryan about when I was in high school and I really wanted to sing 'Defying Gravity.' The other students in my drama class and the teachers, when we were putting on this talent show, they wouldn't let me sing it because I was a boy and it was a girl's song. And then that was made [into] an episode."

And star Chord Overstreet's (Sam) plump lips even worked their way into a storyline...and song, called "Trouty Mouth."

During a Paleyfest panel, Overstreet said, "I never even realized my lips were anything until the jokes started coming. And they wrote that freakin' song!"

While he ultimately didn't snag the role of Finn (his first audition ever!), Darren Criss ended up becoming one of the biggest breakout stars of the series when he made his debut as Head Warbler Blaine Anderson in season two. His first scene, which featured his performance of Katy Perry's "Teenage Dream," set up one of the show's most popular couples, Klaine (Kurt and Blaine), but also delivered one of Glee's most successful singles of all-time, debuting at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

Criss, one of the stars and creators of the popular YouTube "A Very Potter Musical" pre-Glee (He played Harry Potter, of course!), was quickly promoted to series regular and became one of the central characters.

And when Murphy was looking to cast the role of serial killer Andrew Cunanan for The Assassination of Gianni Versace: American Crime Story, he surprised many when he chose Criss, crediting his turn on Broadway in Hedwig and the Angry Inch.

"I just knew he could do it," Murphy revealed to EW. "More than that, I knew that he was super hungry and ambitious. I think people thought of Darren as a musical comedy star first. But, when I saw Hedwig, I knew he was capable of great darkness."

Criss' performance on the FX hit series earned him a Golden Globe, Emmy and SAG Award.

While she would go on to become one of the show's most beloved stars, Heather Morris was actually brought in by the show's choreographer just to teach Colfer how to do the "Single Ladies" dance because she was one of Beyoncé's back-up dancers. Producers then decided to cast her as a background player when they needed a third cheerleader, but they quickly realized they had a secret weapon in Morris, who had a knack for tossing out one-liners "(Did you know dolphins are just gay sharks?") and became a fan-favorite. She was promoted to series regular in season two, becoming the focus of the  Britney Spears tribute episode and one-half of one of the show's most popular couples with Naya Rivera's Santana.

For the fifth season, Morris became a recurring guest star after getting pregnant in real-life, with the actress choosing not to return as a full-time cast member.

At the height of its fame, it seemed like everyone appeared on Glee or wanted to appear on Glee. Some of the show's biggest guest star gets included Gwyneth Paltrow, John Stamos, Helen Mirren (via voiceover), Carol Burnett, Kate Hudson, Lindsay Lohan, Ricky Martin, Sarah Jessica Parker and Whoopi Goldberg, among many, many more.

Still, there were some announced guest stars who never ended up Gleeking out: Javier Bardem was supposed to play a rock star who befriends Artie, which never came to fruition. Anne Hathaway was set to play Kurt's lesbian aunt, but never popped up.

Jennifer Lopez also met with producers, but it never ended up materializing.

After tributes to Madonna and Lady Gaga, Glee staged its most successful tribute episode: in season two: "Britney/Brittany," an homage to Britney Spears. (They did a second Brit tribute episode in season four.)

It was [Britney's] idea," Murphy said of the pop icon's response to the honor. "I think she loves what the show's about, paying tribute to pop culture in a very loving, respectful, kind way. She responded to that."

Unlike Madonna and Gaga though, Spears actually appeared as herself in the episode.

"I loved it! Thank you guys SO much for making this happen!" the "I'm A Slave 4 U" singer tweeted.

And Spears was particularly taken with Morris, writing, "Awww Heather Morris is sooo cute! Brittany S Pearce. Ha! She was so fun to work with and was really sweet in person."

It was a major moment for Morris, who idolized Spears growing up.

"She was my idol from, like, age 12 to 16," Morris told TV Week. "I sang to her [songs] in my living room and danced to her—I learned all her moves. And I had my talent shows and I lip-synced to her. I just kept flashing back to growing up and being obsessed with her."

Glee was so popular that the main cast went on a national tour from 2010-11, selling out almost all of their 40 dates. (Eventually it went overseas as well, visiting European cities.)

"The response of the fans to our little show has been so immediate and so gratifying, we wanted to get out and thank them live and in person," Murphy said when the tour was announced. "And what show lends itself more to a concert than Glee?"

The tour would go on to gross $40 million, and resulted in the two-week theatrical release of Glee: The 3D Concert Movie, using footage from the cast's concert in New Jersey.

As for their music sales, the show's 16 soundtrack albums and six compilation albums had sold over 7.9 million copies by 2015, while their songs had been downloaded over 45 million times and sold 53 million copies.

You can't stay in high school, even when you're attending TV high school. Still, fans were shocked when hen Murphy told THR that the series' main trio Michele, Monteith and Colfer would not be returning for season four after their class graduated from McKinley. Rumors of a potential New York-set spinoff being explored by the producers surfaced, which would find Rachel and Kurt trying to make their Broadway dreams come true in the Big Apple.

"You can keep them on the show for six years and people will criticize you for not being realistic," Murphy said at the time, "or you can be really true to life and say when they started the show they were very clearly sophomores and they should graduate at the end of their senior year."

But the trio ended up staying on Glee, which focused on their post-college plans while also introducing new students into the mix at McKinley, with the network's then president telling reporters ahead of season four, "There will not be a Glee spinoff."

Still, season four presented a shake-up for the show, with Murphy telling Vulture he gave the original cast members the choice to exit the series if they wanted after their characters graduated. "I said to them, 'Anybody who wants to stay on the show will stay on the show,'" he explained. Almost everyone stayed but many dropped down to recurring or guest star status.

During Glee's third season, The Glee Project kicked off on Oxygen, which found the contestants competing for a role on the main show.

From its two season-run, Glee brought four contestants over, including season one's winners Samuel Larsen and Damian McGinty Jr., as well as runner-ups Lindsay Pearce and Alex Newell. Blake Jenner, the winner of season two, became a series regular in season five, while the runner-up Ali Stroker made an unexpected guest appearance in season four.

One of the show's breakout stars, winning a Golden Globe for his turn as Kurt, Colfer went on to write an episode of Glee in season five, later admitting he was terrified to take on the challenge despite writing several novels, as well as the film adaptation of his book Struck By Lighting.

"When they first approached me I said, absolutely not," he said during a Paleyfest panel. "I'm not putting words into my costars' mouths. There was a lot of pressure."

His onscreen paramour Darren Criss also penned something for Glee during the show's run, writing an original song for the series finale called "This Time."

"I basically wrote a love note to the entire experience," Criss explained of the song, which Michele sang in the episode. "Having Lea sing it to me is one of the most special moments of my career."

It was just as special for Michele, who said, "Darren gave me the greatest gift. Honestly. That was the day I fell to my knees and cried. I literally had to call my mother to come [get me]. It's so special, it was the most amazing memory."

The song would go on to be nominated for an Emmy.

In 2011, a Glee extra/fan found herself in hot water when she shared major spoilers on Twitter, revealing most of the major happenings at the prom. Co-creator Brad Falchuk put her on blast, responding, "Who are you to spoil something talented people have spent months to create?"

He then added, "hope you're qualified to do something besides work in entertainment."

The leaker Nicole Crowther, then 2, received "very, very hateful messages" from fans and said she was "black-balled" by every agency in town.

"I had no idea it would even come close to anything it's been," she told E! News. "I regret it and I can totally understand, not only where the fans are coming from, but why Brad and other people from Fox are furious with me. I can understand their point of view."

A few years later, the show had another Twitter scandal when someone hacked Colfer's account and tweeted he was leaving the show. "Due to personal issues, I have been let go from the cast of GLEE. Explanations will come shortly..." the message read.

After the mass hysteria from Klaine fans subsided when the show's rep denied Colfer was leaving the show, the actor appeared on Good Morning America, calling the hack "very upsetting."

"Some jerk hacked me," he said. "It was a pain, it really was."

In her 2016 memoir, Sorry Not Sorry: Dreams, Mistakes and Growing Up, Rivera revealed she got an abortion during the show's run.

In late 2010, Naya discovered she was pregnant just weeks after breaking up with actor Ryan Dorsey, whom she later wed in 2014 and is the father of her son, Josey Dorsey (they divorced in 2018).

She chose not share the news with Dorsey at the time, instead choosing to focus on her career; she terminated the pregnancy during a day off from filming an episode of Glee.

"I think every woman should have the right to choose, and it scares me to think of a world where the decision of whether to have a child is not her choice to make," she wrote.

After Monteith's sudden and tragic death from combined drug intoxication in 2013 at the age of 31, questions arose about how Glee would handle his passing and Finn's absence on the show (with Murphy telling E! News they even considered ending  the series).

After taking an extended hiatus, Glee addressed Monteith's death in "The Quarterback," a beautiful tribute episode that revealed Finn had died. It was an emotional and somber hour of television, both on-screen and off as each cast member was given a change to honor Monteith in the episode.

"Almost everything in that episode is from the first take of every performance because the actors and the crew had a really hard time shooting it,' Murphy said at the time. "I've never seen a crew that you can't continue shooting because they've left the room sobbing. It was very hard. I struggled even working on it because what they felt, not just about Finn but Cory."

The episode ended with Michele, Monteith's girlfriend, singing Bob Dylan's "Make You Feel My Love," and Rachel returning to McKinley to hang a plaque in the choir room featuring a picture of Finn and a quote from him that reads: "The show must go...all over the place...or something."

Matthew Morrison said of the filming, "[Lea] had one of the first songs we filmed for the episode and she did it so beautifully and after, she said something like, 'It can't be harder for anyone else than it was for me.' So, we knew we had to show up because our leader stepped forward and kind of gave permission to all of us to do it. I don't think we could have done it without her."

In an In Memoriam piece penned for Entertainment Weekly in 2013, Murphy revealed the ending he and the writers originally envisioned for Finchel's journey on the show.

"Rachel comes back to Ohio, fulfilled and yet not, and walks into Finn's glee club," he explained. "'What are you doing here?' he would ask. 'I'm home,' she would reply. Fade out. The End."

Three of Michele's 16 tattoos are Glee-related: Michele showed off her "Finn" tattoo when she posed naked for the cover of Women's Health U.K., a tattoo Rachel had gotten on the show as a tribute to Finn after his death. Michele also has the No. 5 in honor of Monteith, which was Finn's football jersey number.

"And one more...for my Quarterback...#5," she captioned the Instagram post debuting her new body ink.

She also has a tiny gold star on her left wrist as a nod to her character Rachel and one of her lines from the pilot episode: "You may laugh because every time I sign my name I put a gold star after it, but it's a metaphor, and metaphors are important. My gold stars are a metaphor for ME being a star."

In an interview with Rolling Stone, Michele revealed she and co-stars Ushkowitz and McHale got matching "Imagine" tattoos on their feet, a nod to The Beatles, during a night out and a few glasses of wine.

"I'm known to be the instigator to do some more risky stuff. So we have little tattoos on our feet now," she said. "It made a lot of sense that night."

Many of the cast members have remained since the series ended in 2015, proving once a Gleek always a Gleek.

Michele and Criss have gone on co-headlining tours together, and Michele performed at Criss' nuptials to longtime girlfriend Mia Swier in February 2019. Criss was also present Michele married Zandy Reich a month later in a ceremony officiated by Murphy. Becca Tobin, who joined Glee in season four and ow stars in E!'s Ladygang, was also present as she and Michele have continued to be best friends in the years since Glee.

When Tobin got married in 2016 Jane Lynch officiated the ceremony, which was a mini-Glee reunion with Michele, McHale, Ushkowitz, Meg Doyle, Michael Hitchcock, Matt Hodgson and Dante Russo all in attendance.

In 2018, Morrison reunited many of the member of New Directions to meet his newborn son, Revel James Makai Morrison. "It's a GLEE-Union!!" Morrison captioned the photo of the gang, including Michele, Rivera, Riley, Morris, Colfer, Criss and more. "What a beautiful night hangin with my old kids & new kid! Ohana..."

In March, some of the Gleeks, including Crazy Rich Asians' Harry Shum Jr., reunited on-screen, competing against each other on Drop the Mic.

James Gunn's new DC universe might be done, but the follow-up to 2025's Superman is still on the way.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It feels like yesterday when we were discussing Superman, the first big-screen entry in James Gunn's rebooted DCU. Now Gunn is out, and Skydance (the company formed by the merger of Warner and Paramount) is already dismantling his grand plans for the DCU.

That means that Man of Tomorrow, which arrives next summer, will be the final entry in Gunn's ambitious, and occasionally divisive, DC experiment. The DCU's first chapter — officially titled 'Gods and Monsters' — gave us Supergirl and Clayface (as well as TV shows like Peacemaker S2 and Lanterns) in the run-up to Clark Kent and Lex Luthor's return.

Man of Tomorrow looks to be upping the stakes from Earthly villains to intergalactic baddies with the introduction of Brainiac, and it may well have been the herald of the first Justice League movie in the rebooted DCU.

Gunn has yet to prove audiences actually care about more than Batman and Supes, which might explain why this follow-up is also an ensemble of sorts. As the Marvel Cinematic Universe prepares to unleash Avengers: Doomsday, Secret Wars, and even a fresh X-Men reboot, their DC counterparts have always struggled to get their dream team off the ground.

We'll never know what might have been, but we can still enjoy Gunn's DC swansong when it lands in 2027. Here's everything we know about James Gunn's Man of Tomorrow.

Man of Tomorrow will be released theatrically in the United States on July 9, 2027. Most international territories are expected to get it around the same time.

Only a few months after Superman's release and successful box office run, DC Studios and Warner Bros. Pictures confirmed the sequel would be coming two years after Clark Kent's return to the big screen.

Man of Tomorrow isn't out yet, but you can watch the rest of the DCU so far (it's pretty good for the most part) in preparation first.

When the movie hits theaters on July 9, 2027, it'll likely remain exclusive to big screens for at least two or three months, depending on how successful it is.

With that said, we know Warner Bros. (now part of Skydance) isn't the most patient when it comes to theatrical runs based on its track record, so the chances are Man of Tomorrow will hit HBO Max sooner rather than later, probably by early autumn 2027.

Watch Superman and the rest of the DCU on HBO Max:

Basic (Ads): $10.99/month or $109.99/yearStandard (No Ads): $18.49/month or $184.99/year Premium (4K): $22.99/month or $229.99/year

No, we're still waiting for the first Man of Tomorrow trailer. Looking at the timeline of Superman's fantastic marketing campaign, however, we can guess the sequel will get a first trailer before 2026 ends, probably in time for Christmas.

Yes, James Gunn has officially confirmed Brainiac is the main threat Earth is facing in Man of Tomorrow. This explains why other heroes will be joining Superman in a fight against the alien mastermind, but the plot is looking a bit more complex.

In typical comic book fashion (and somewhat reminiscent of Thor: The Dark World), the main hook in Man of Tomorrow appears to be a reluctant alliance between the first movie's villain, Lex Luthor, and Kal-El (aka Clark Kent). "Enemies to allies" is always a fun dynamic to have in a sequel, especially when stars David Corenswet (Superman) and Nicholas Hoult (Lex Luthor) delivered strong and memorable performances the first time around.

The actual plot remains under wraps, but we can guess Brainiac — one of DC's biggest and most iconic alien villains — will be a tough nut to crack, thus requiring some sort of unofficial team-up that will include returning heroes like Mister Terrific, Guy Gardner, Hawkgirl, John Stewart, Blue Beetle, and even Kara Zor-El (Supergirl). There are other names circling the project that could lead to even bigger appearances, but don't expect to learn much about them before the movie's marketing kicks off.

Why should you care about Brainiac? Well, he's a super-intelligent techno-organic alien from the planet Colu with an obsession with knowledge and self-improvement. A perfect foe for Luthor, Earth's greatest mind, but also a breath of fresh air for Superman, who's been stuck battling either Kryptonian menaces or just Luthor too long on the big screen.

As a direct continuation of Superman, Man of Tomorrow is bringing back plenty of actors in both main and supporting roles, including:

New cast members with publicly announced (or previously established) characters include:

Last but not least, we also know Adria Arjona, Andre Royo, Matthew Lillard, and Sinqua Walls are part of the cast, but their parts remain a secret for now.

Much of the current Man of Tomorrow speculation centers on Adria Arjona's role in the story. While many have theorized she could be playing Wonder Woman — something that neither Gunn nor Arjona has straight-up denied — the earlier reports and rumors suggested she could be Maxima.

Such a role would fit Gunn's penchant for throwing lesser-known comic book heroes and villains into his movies wherever possible. If you're not an avid reader or longtime DC fan, all you need to know is that Maxima is an alien conqueror from the planet Almerac obsessed with Superman as her perfect mate and king. She's also morally ambiguous, at least when she first appeared, so that makes her a particularly interesting character to bring in for a more complex and nuanced sequel.

With Brainiac spearheading the roster of new DC icons joining Man of Tomorrow, it also isn't hard to imagine another alien figure factoring into the plot, though the flick is getting extremely crowded as it is.

Yes, James Gunn is the sole writer and director of Man of Tomorrow.

Despite his previous role as co-chairman and co-CEO of DC Studios, Gunn is extremely hands-on when it comes to most DCU projects. In fact, it seems he had already begun working on his next movie after Man of Tomorrow, though his unceremonious exit will almost certainly mean the end of those plans.

He's also co-producing alongside Peter Safran, who was also ousted in November 2026's DC Studios shakeup.

The rest of the crew includes Sam McCurdy (Peacemaker, Shogun) as cinematographer, Fred Raskin (Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3, Supergirl) as editor, and David Fleming (Superman, Anaconda) as the main composer, among others.

#814. Mysterious gas leaks suggest Mars may still be volcanically alive

Mars may not be as geologically inactive as it appears. New evidence from mysterious gas emissions near an enormous Martian volcano suggests that heat and volcanic processes could still be present deep beneath the planet's surface.

Researchers have identified unusual concentrations of hydrogen chloride gas above fractures in the Alba Mons volcanic region. The findings suggest that gases from the planet's interior may be escaping through cracks in the surface, potentially revealing volcanic activity that has remained hidden until now.

An international team led by Alexander Trokhimovskiy believes the gas could originate from hot magma underground. If confirmed, this would indicate that Mars still has dormant volcanic systems capable of releasing gases to the surface.

The European Space Agency's ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) first detected hydrogen chloride in the Martian atmosphere in findings reported in 2021. On Earth, hydrogen chloride is frequently released through openings connected to magma, raising the possibility that similar processes could be occurring on Mars.

"Our findings suggest that Mars has retained enough internal heat to support volcanic activity until recently, and possibly still does," says Daniel Mège, Professor at the Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences and co-lead author of the study published in Science Advances.

Mysterious Gas Emissions Defy Mars' Seasonal Pattern

The researchers noticed something unusual during early summer in the Martian northern hemisphere. Hydrogen chloride concentrations were unexpectedly elevated in a particular region, even though the gas normally becomes scarce at that time of year.

Hydrogen chloride levels on Mars generally follow a seasonal cycle. They typically peak during northern winter before declining to very low levels in summer. Scientists believe much of this behavior is associated with the planet's dust and water cycles.

However, the observations revealed a striking exception. Elevated hydrogen chloride repeatedly appeared in early summer over volcanic fractures on the slopes of Alba Mons. The unusual timing and consistent location suggested that something beyond ordinary atmospheric chemistry might be responsible.

Mars is home to the largest volcanoes in the Solar System, but scientists still do not know whether volcanic processes remain active beneath their surfaces.

Images taken from orbit indicate that some Martian volcanoes experienced eruptions within the past few million years. Instruments on the surface have also recorded marsquakes, demonstrating that the planet continues to experience seismic activity.

Together, these observations suggest that Mars may retain some of its geological energy. However, scientists have never directly observed a new volcanic eruption or fresh lava flow on the planet, leaving the question of present-day volcanism unresolved.

Fresh Cracks Reveal Clues to Hidden Volcanic Heat

To investigate the unusual gas concentrations, the research team combined atmospheric measurements with detailed observations of the Martian surface.

The Atmospheric Chemistry Suite aboard TGO uses infrared spectrometers to identify gases in the atmosphere. These instruments detected hydrogen chloride concentrated in a relatively small area shortly after the disappearance of winter frost.

Researchers then examined the same region using the orbiter's CaSSIS camera. The images revealed narrow fractures that appeared relatively fresh, with some extending hundreds of meters across the surface. Unusual changes in surface color were also visible around the cracks.

"The Trace Gas Orbiter was able to find the smoking gun. It was like looking for a needle in a haystack. It's truly amazing that it spotted a handful of molecules from a perhaps intermittent source, whilst moving continuously along its orbit to monitor the whole Martian atmosphere," explains Daniel.

One possible explanation is that gases originating from magma deep underground travel upward through these fractures. On Earth, comparable volcanic openings are known as fumaroles.

The researchers propose that extremely cold Martian winters, when temperatures can fall to -120°C, allow ice to seal the fractures and temporarily prevent gases from escaping. As temperatures rise in early summer, the ice sublimates, changing directly into vapor and potentially opening pathways for underground gases to reach the atmosphere.

The discoloration observed around the fractures could also be significant. It may result from minerals or other substances deposited by escaping gases, similar to the deposits commonly found around fumaroles (volcanic gas vents) on Earth.

Although the connection between the gas emissions and volcanic fractures appeared promising, the researchers needed to rule out other explanations.

"Looking at the spatial distribution of the seeping, it became instantly obvious to me that there was something volcanic behind it, but it had to be demonstrated," concedes Daniel.

The team carefully evaluated the chemical reactions that could produce hydrogen chloride in the Martian atmosphere, including processes unrelated to volcanism.

"A huge part of the work consisted of examining all the possible chemical processes going on in the Martian atmosphere. We needed to be rigorous, critical and creative to explain the presence of hydrogen chloride. The data were complex, but also excellent brain food," adds Daniel.

After examining the atmospheric and geological evidence together, the researchers proposed that the gas could be escaping from a dormant magma chamber beneath Alba Mons. Such a chamber would form part of an underground volcanic system that could continue releasing gases even without producing visible eruptions.

Hidden Volcanic Activity Could Help Mars Support Life

The implications may extend beyond understanding the planet's geological history. Volcanic gases could also provide clues about how Mars evolved and whether it ever supported environments suitable for life.

In the distant past, gases released from magma, including hydrogen chloride, may have helped create a denser atmosphere and warmer conditions. Those conditions could have allowed liquid water to remain across large portions of the Martian surface.

Volcanic activity might also create habitable environments underground. If rising magma or lava comes into contact with groundwater, the interaction can produce warm hydrothermal systems. Such environments could provide both chemical energy and protection from the harsh conditions on the surface.

"Looking for Martian life in the seeping fissures of the Alba Mons region would make a lot of sense. If hydrothermal systems are active, they could contain the ingredients and energy needed for microorganisms to develop, and shield microorganisms from the hostile and changing environment above the surface," ponders Daniel.

Although the findings do not establish that Mars is currently erupting or that life exists beneath its surface, they offer an intriguing new reason to investigate the volcanic fractures around Alba Mons.

"These findings may prove to be TGO's greatest success yet," highlights Colin Wilson, ESA's project scientist for the ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter.

Liftoff is scheduled for 5:45 p.m. ET today (Nov. 13).

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Update for 6:25 p.m. ET: SpaceX has launched the Starship Flight 15 mission, but did skip the first stage Super Heavy booster landing. See launch video and our full Starship Flight 15 liftoff wrap.

SpaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live.

Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). SpaceX plans to bring both of Starship's stages back to Starbase for a catch by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — something it has never done before.

You can watch it all live here at Space.com. And there should be a lot to see: Starship Flight 15 will last more than 22 hours, if all goes according to plan.

Starship consists of two elements: a huge booster known as Super Heavy and an upper-stage spacecraft called Starship, or Ship for short. Both are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first in the world of orbital spaceflight.

The rapidity of Starship's reuse hinges heavily on SpaceX's recovery strategy: Returning both vehicles directly to the launch mount will enable much faster inspection, refurbishment and reflight, the company has said.

SpaceX has already caught Super Heavy, pulling the feat off on three previous Starship test flights. But it has never tried to do so with Ship, which flies farther and faster than the booster and is therefore a more challenging vehicle to recover.

So today's flight is a pretty big deal for SpaceX.

"If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," the company wrote in a Flight 15 mission description.

The action will unspool over two days, if all goes to plan. Super Heavy will return to Starbase for a touchdown just 6.5 minutes after launch, but Ship will continue on to low Earth orbit.

The upper stage will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites, during a 42-minute stretch beginning about 35 minutes after liftoff. This will be just the second batch of V3 spacecraft to reach orbit, after the 26 that went up on Flight 14 on Sept. 28.

Ship will then stay aloft for nearly a full day. The mission plan calls for the upper stage to return to Starbase for its chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), about 22.5 hours after liftoff.

There's no guarantee things will go according to plan, however. SpaceX will call off a Ship catch if the vehicle experiences any issues during Flight 15. If something crops up, the company will steer Ship to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, either near Hawaii or off the coast of Chile.

So it'll be a busy weekend for SpaceX, and for space fans who want to keep tabs on the mission. And we can help you out there, with our Flight 15 updates page.

Michael Wall is the Spaceflight and Tech Editor for Space.com and joined the team in 2010. He primarily covers human and robotic spaceflight, military space, and exoplanets, but has been known to dabble in the space art beat. His book about the search for alien life, "Out There," was published on Nov. 13, 2018. Before becoming a science writer, Michael worked as a herpetologist and wildlife biologist. He has a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology from the University of Sydney, Australia, a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona, and a graduate certificate in science writing from the University of California, Santa Cruz. To find out what his latest project is, you can follow Michael on Twitter.

#810. Has Trafford replaced Pickford as England No 1?

James Trafford has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026

As he was mobbed by his England team-mates for a late double save that secured a memorable 3-2 win against world champions Spain, the debate that followed about who the country's number one is was inevitable.

The Leeds keeper was given his chance to show England boss Thomas Tuchel what he could do again - and he absolutely took it.

On his fifth England cap the 24-year-old enjoyed a magnificent performance in Madrid as his side handed the hosts their first loss in 43 matches.

Trafford made four key saves in the final 12 minutes of the game, including an incredible double stop to first deny a Lamine Yamal curler and then dive again to his right to keep out Fermin Lopez from close range.

Last week Tuchel had made it clear that Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford was his number one.

But after full-time in Spain Tuchel told ITV Sport "there's no number one" and Trafford had "a brilliant match".

So, following his performance on Sunday night, is Trafford now likely to oust Pickford as England's go-to goalkeeper?

Is Trafford 'closing the gap' on Pickford?

Despite being just 24 years old Trafford has already been England's most expensive goalkeeper by transfer fee... twice.

Trafford returned to his boyhood Manchester City from Burnley for a Â£31m fee in 2025 and then left the Etihad for Leeds for Â£45m this summer - having been limited to being Pep Guardiola's 'cup goalkeeper'.

Given the downturn in form of their current goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, many City fans may well be wishing Trafford had stayed. Their loss is Leeds' - and maybe England's - gain.

At Leeds he has found his form and this season ranks first among the 52 goalkeepers who have played at least 10 games in Europe's big five leagues by save percentage (81.4%).

He has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026, and has rotated with Pickford across the Three Lions' five matches since the World Cup.

Pickford has started against Czech Republic and Croatia twice whereas Trafford has played against Czech Republic and started both England's matches with Spain, home and away.

After England's win in Madrid, which was the first time Spain had lost in the city in 39 years, Trafford's double-save was praised by his Three Lions team-mate Declan Rice.

"Everything happened so quick so for him to make two in the space of two seconds is massive," he told ITV. "A massive night for him."

Spain manager Luis de la Fuente agreed. He said: "We did generate some chances but England's goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last 10 or 15 minutes."

After the double-save several England players ran over to celebrate with Trafford.

And on Tuchel's decision to rotate between his two keepers former Manchester United captain Roy Keane told ITV: "I think it's smart management.

"This is the perfect time for Trafford to come in, against top players, and show what he's capable of doing."

Social media has been full of the 'England number one' debate since, with many suggesting this was a moment that marked the changing of the guard.

Could Tuchel really now not start with Trafford for England's Nations League quarter-finals? Only time will tell.

What about Pickford though? England's undisputed first choice for almost 10 years has rarely let his country down.

The 32-year-old has won 94 caps for England since making his debut in a 0-0 draw with Germany in 2017 and during his time as number one England have reached two World Cup semi-finals and two Euros finals.

According to Opta stats, Pickford has only made two errors leading to goals across his England career, with 46 clean sheets and a 74.3% save ratio.

And since the start of the 2024-25 season, only Arsenal's title-winning keeper David Raya has more clean sheets in the league than Pickford at Everton.

"We saw the last selections and all thought Jordan Pickford's place is under threat and James Trafford is going to be the next number one. I don't think Thomas Tuchel saw it as starkly or simply as that," said former England number one goalkeeper Paul Robinson to BBC Sport before England's win against Spain,

"It's a conversation that will definitely take place down the road, but not now. Jordan is England's first choice, in my opinion, rightfully so given his consistency and performances over such a long period.

"This is a debate and conversation for the future definitely because Father Time catches up with everyone eventually and the manager needs to have a contingency plan, but Jordan Pickford very much remains number one and Thomas Tuchel has said as much.

"I don't think Jordan Pickford is under threat for his jersey on a permanent basis any time soon, irrespective of the next selection."

This isn't a debate that is going away any time soon. But having two goalkeepers genuinely competing for that number one shirt can only be to England's benefit.

#809. Ancient Siberian tomb reveals surprising secrets of cannabis use 2,800 years ago

A remarkable discovery in a nearly 2,800-year-old Siberian tomb has provided the oldest directly dated archaeological evidence that people used cannabis for its intoxicating effects. By examining ancient cannabis seeds and chemical traces preserved in human hair, researchers have uncovered new clues about the role of the plant in prehistoric burial rituals.

Cannabis is among the most widely used psychoactive plants in the modern world, but tracing its use thousands of years into the past presents a major archaeological challenge. Flowers, leaves, and resins tend to decompose over time, leaving little physical evidence behind. Ancient communities also relied on cannabis for practical purposes, including producing fiber and oil, making it difficult to distinguish these uses from medicinal or recreational consumption.

An international team led by Dr. Gino Caspari, affiliated with the Institute of Archaeological Sciences at the University of Bern and the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology, investigated an elaborate tomb in the Republic of Tyva in southern Siberia. The burial site belonged to prominent members of the Scythians, a culture known for its skilled horseback riders who inhabited the vast Eurasian steppe.

Ancient Siberian Tomb Contains 1,000 Cannabis Seeds

During the investigation, researchers recovered approximately 1,000 cannabis seeds from the tomb. They used radiocarbon dating to determine the age of six individual seeds. Combined with other dating evidence, the results indicate that the seeds were deposited in the burial site during the early eighth century B.C.

"The seeds show that cannabis played an important role in the rituals surrounding the burial," says Caspari, an archaeologist and the study's lead author.

The researchers also analyzed human hair preserved in the tomb's central burial chamber. Chemical evidence in several samples pointed to cannabis consumption, providing a crucial connection between the plant remains and the people buried at the site.

"This study is particularly insightful because it combines the analysis of plant remains with molecular traces in the human body," says Caspari.

The findings were published in the journal Science.

Chemical Traces in Ancient Hair Reveal Cannabis Use

Although the cannabis seeds were remarkably well preserved, their presence alone could not establish whether the plant was used for its mind-altering effects. The seeds probably came from wild cannabis plants, and researchers could not determine whether people had deliberately cultivated them for their psychoactive properties.

The strongest evidence came from the preserved human hair. Using high-resolution mass spectrometry and other analytical techniques, the team identified clear chemical signals consistent with cannabinol (CBN) in several samples.

CBN can form when tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the primary compound responsible for cannabis intoxication, undergoes oxidation. The researchers also detected weaker signals that matched the mass of THC, further supporting the possibility that the individuals had consumed cannabis.

While these chemical findings indicate cannabis use, they cannot reveal how much was consumed or exactly how the compounds entered the body. The individuals may have inhaled cannabis smoke or consumed the plant in another way, but the available evidence cannot establish a particular method.

Other archaeological discoveries from later periods in Central Asia provide clearer evidence of cannabis inhalation. At those sites, researchers have identified cannabinoid residues on heated stones and inside vessels, pointing to the use of heat to release compounds that could be inhaled.

"The molecular traces in the hair and the cannabis seeds come from the same grave and suggest that cannabis was used for its intoxicating properties," says Caspari, who conducts research at the Institute of Archaeological Sciences at the University of Bern and the Max Planck Institute for Geoanthropology in Jena (Germany).

Cannabis, Horse Sacrifices, and Ancient Burial Rituals

The cannabis evidence was discovered within an elaborate ceremonial burial site, suggesting that the plant may have been connected to important Scythian funerary traditions.

"In this princely tomb, the burials were accompanied by extensive horse sacrifices and, most likely, human sacrifices as well," says Gino Caspari.

Earlier research at the site identified the remains of 18 horses that had been deliberately positioned on the burial mound. Continued excavations have since uncovered evidence of several dozen more sacrificed horses, along with scattered human bones.

These discoveries reveal the extraordinary scale of the burial ceremonies and provide important context for understanding why cannabis may have been included among the materials deposited in the tomb.

Oldest Directly Dated Evidence of Cannabis Intoxication

Taken together, the seeds and chemical traces in human hair represent the oldest directly dated archaeological evidence currently known for cannabis use associated with intoxication.

However, several questions remain unanswered. The researchers cannot determine how much THC the ancient cannabis contained, whether the plants were particularly potent, or whether Scythian communities had begun deliberately selecting or cultivating cannabis varieties with higher concentrations of psychoactive compounds.

To investigate these questions, the team is now studying genetic material recovered from the ancient plant remains. The unusually good preservation of the cannabis DNA could provide valuable insights into how humans domesticated the plant and how it spread across different regions over thousands of years.

"We have already begun sequencing some of the plant samples," says Gino Caspari. "DNA preservation is excellent in this case. This will help us learn more about the history of the domestication and spread of this crop soon."

#808. As El Niño builds, studies of extreme marine heatwaves must start now

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Alistair J. Hobday is a chief research scientist at CSIRO Environment, Hobart, Australia.

Kathryn E. Smith is a research fellow at the Marine Biological Association, Plymouth, UK.

Claire M. Spillman is a principal research scientist at the Bureau of Meteorology, Melbourne, Australia.

Karen Filbee-Dexter is a Future Fellow at the UWA Oceans Institute and School of Biological Sciences, University of Western Australia, Perth, Australia, and a principal scientist at the Institute of Marine Research, Flødevigen Research Station, His, Norway.

Neil J. Holbrook is a professor of ocean and climate dynamics at the Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies and the ARC Centre of Excellence for the Weather of the 21st Century, University of Tasmania, Hobart, Australia.

Caroline Rowland is head of ocean cryosphere and climate at the Met Office, Exeter, UK.

Dan A. Smale is a senior research fellow at the Marine Biological Association, Plymouth, UK.

Grant Smith is a senior research scientist at the Bureau of Meteorology, Melbourne, Australia.

Mads S. Thomsen is an adjunct professor at the UWA Oceans Institute and School of Biological Sciences, University of Western Australia, Perth, Australia, and an associate professor in the School of Biological Sciences, University of Canterbury, Christchurch, New Zealand.

Thomas Wernberg is a laureate professor at the UWA Oceans Institute and School of Biological Sciences, University of Western Australia, Perth, Australia, and principal scientist at the Institute of Marine Research, Flødevigen Research Station, His, Norway.

Alex Sen Gupta is a professor in the Climate Change Research Centre and the Centre for Marine Science and Innovation, University of New South Wales, Sydney, Australia.

Coral nurseries, such as this one in French Polynesia, can be used to study the resilience of the organisms in real-world settings. Credit: Alexis Rosenfeld/Getty

With temperatures in the Pacific Ocean at record-high levels and forecasts of an extreme El Niño climate event, intense marine heatwaves are expected around the world in the coming year1,2. Scientists must prepare to study these extreme conditions now, so that managers of marine resources and decision makers can develop and implement response strategies and communities can plan for a hotter future.

The super El Niño is cooking coral reefs — can lullabies and probiotics save them?

The super El Niño is cooking coral reefs — can lullabies and probiotics save them?

El Niño is part of a recurring natural cycle in Earth’s climate in which warmer waters in the central and eastern Pacific alter ocean and atmospheric circulation, affecting weather worldwide. Marine heatwaves associated with El Niño provide opportunities to study ecosystems under real-world stress conditions and on scales that cannot be replicated in a laboratory.

Marine heatwaves can be forecast weeks or months ahead, giving researchers time to design field studies, deploy instruments and collect baseline data. Investigations can be designed to test theories and improve our understanding of ecological processes, thresholds and recovery mechanisms in a rapidly warming ocean.

Such knowledge can inform decisions about how to manage marine resources, such as whether to close fisheries. Much has been learnt about marine heatwaves since the last El Niño, in 2023–24 (see ‘Hot water’). But these lessons need to be consolidated and scaled up into consistent, long-term preparedness plans.

Source: Climate Reanalyzer (CC-BY-4.0); go.nature.com/4zae69a

Fortunately, effective approaches established in one place can be extended to others. Australia is a leader in developing early-warning systems and response plans for adaptation to a more extreme ocean climate. Other nations (including the United Kingdom, the United States, New Zealand and Peru) have improved their awareness of these events and put in place observation systems, forecasts and briefings, policy mechanisms and (in a few cases) adaptation measures.

But further action is needed, particularly in locations that have previously been unaffected by severe marine heatwaves. Here, we highlight seven priorities in increasing marine heatwave preparedness.

Seasonal forecasts with lead times of several months are now being delivered in various regions, including the United States3 and Australia4, and such systems are being developed in the United Kingdom and New Zealand5 and for the Mediterranean Sea6.

Forecasting relies on physical and statistical models to predict probable ocean temperatures7. Data from sustained surface and below-surface observations are essential for initializing models and verifying predictions, building users’ confidence in forecasts.

The super El Niño is more than a climate shock — it’s a health one, too

The super El Niño is more than a climate shock — it’s a health one, too

But managers want to know more precisely what the duration and intensity of a marine heatwave is expected to be. Forecasts become less accurate the further ahead they look and at fine spatial scales, such as along coasts. Improved ocean monitoring, a better understanding of the drivers of marine heatwaves and continued refinements of model physics are needed to improve forecast accuracy7.

Advances in machine learning are expected to be transformative. Next-generation models that incorporate ocean physics might be able to predict unprecedented marine heatwaves more accurately than current technologies can. Downscaling global climate models to inshore regions using machine-learning techniques could also increase the usefulness of forecasts in places where most marine-resource users operate.

Planning for and communication about impending marine heatwaves are also improving1. In 2023, engagement was piecemeal and often only in response to events that were already in progress. Activities are now more proactive and structured.

Coordinated briefings that translate forecasts into action provide ways of engaging with affected groups and planning ahead. Such communication strategies should be implemented around the world4,8. National briefings provide a broad overview of marine heatwave risks and impacts. Regional and industry specialists can provide further local advice.

For example, Australia’s national marine climate briefing series4 has been running since 2023. Similar meetings (led or contributed to by some of us) have taken place for the western Pacific Ocean (G.S.) and in the United Kingdom (C.R.), Brazil (K.E.S.), Singapore (C.M.S.) and New Zealand (C.M.S.).

Seafood-producing firms and conservation managers need a menu of actions to choose from when a marine heatwave looms. Options include adjusting collection strategies, temporarily closing fisheries and modifying aquaculture operations1.

Australia has developed regional and industry-specific response plans for marine heatwaves8. Response teams for fisheries are active during warming events and provide coordinated mechanisms for assessment, communication and management actions4,9.

Impacts of marine heatwaves are being monitored in restored giant kelp forests in Tasmania, Australia.Credit: Scott Ling/University of Tasmania

Early-warning systems and interagency coordination are key components of timely responses. Industry has also adopted operating protocols to reduce the impacts of marine heatwaves on animal health and food-product quality. For example, abalone fisheries in New South Wales have changed how sea snails (Haliotis spp.) are fished, handled and prepared for live export10. Other regions could benefit from similar plans4.

For example, fishing of Peruvian anchoveta (Engraulis ringens), the source of around 20% of fishmeal and fish oil globally, has already been curbed by the current El Niño. In 2023, the fishery had to be closed, resulting in an estimated loss11 of US$1.4 billion. This year, an alert in February prompted Peruvian authorities to bring the fishing season forwards by two weeks and reduce the total allowable catch of anchoveta and white anchovy (Anchoa nasus) by more than 30% to 1.9 million tonnes. This meant that fisheries could catch about 450,000 tonnes before the heatwave intensified and the season was ended in May.

In 2023, marine heatwave preparedness was recognized as inadequate in most regions. The emphasis then was mainly on raising risk awareness in sectors such as fisheries and aquaculture1. However, these and other industries need to adapt to a changing ocean, too.

Awareness has now grown among sectors and institutions, and behaviours have begun to change. For example, Australian marine climate briefings draw engagement from aquaculture and fishery managers, marine tourism operators, policymakers, researchers and individual fishers4.

In the United States, forecasts of marine heatwaves trigger advice to fishers regarding increases in interactions with marine mammals as the overlap between animals’ hunting grounds and deployed fishing gear expands, which can result in fishery closures. Coral-reef managers involved in restoration efforts can scale back replanting efforts and start collecting genetic material.

The worst El Niño in recorded history is brewing — here’s how governments must prepare

The worst El Niño in recorded history is brewing — here’s how governments must prepare

In the Mediterranean Sea, limiting diving tourism at coral reefs to minimize damage during marine heatwaves has been proposed, mirroring practices that were adopted in Asia during the 2023–24 marine heatwaves11.

In the Cook Islands’ black-pearl industry, seasonal forecasts have been proposed for supporting decisions around adaptive management aimed at reducing the thermal stress of oysters. These include increased reliance on hatchery production under controlled temperature conditions and preferential harvesting of pearls during cooler periods of the year.

In the United Kingdom, a national marine heatwave network and code of best practice have been established, enabling the exchange of transdisciplinary knowledge. Similar transfers of experience, capacity and lessons learnt between jurisdictions can accelerate preparedness globally and help to embed risk management into routine decision-making processes4.

The 2023 El Niño led to calls to strengthen monitoring and research capacity to improve the detection of, understanding of and response to marine heatwaves. Observation networks are now becoming a core component of preparedness and response plans, providing the information needed to support forecasting, impact assessment, management interventions and long-term adaptation strategies12.

Targeted uses of gliders and intensified monitoring strategies can bolster research, situational awareness and management decisions12. Research has expanded into understanding ecological resilience and adaptation. For example, genetic studies are identifying traits that might enhance the capacity of key fishery or habitat-forming species13 to persist under increasing thermal stress.

Researchers in Florida are studying corals obtained from local reefs as part of restoration efforts.Credit: Chandan Khanna/AFP via Getty

#807. How Frank can restore reputation and save Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace are Thomas Frank's third London club after previous spells with Brentford and Tottenham

"When the time is right I will look forward to my return as a manager, ready to embrace the job with great energy and dedication," said Thomas Frank in June.

That time is now after the Dane was confirmed as the new manager of Crystal Palace, who are two points and a goal difference deficit away from safety at the bottom of the Premier League.

Former boss Pierre Sage was sacked last week after just 16 league and cup games.

The role offers Frank an opportunity to rebuild his reputation after he was sacked by Tottenham in February after eight months.

Frank described it as "an honour" to be "in charge of this fantastic football club" as Palace announced his arrival on a deal running to June 2029.

"Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League," Frank told Palace's website.

"I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them."

Palace chairman Steve Parish said Frank was the "perfect fit for our club".

But how big is the challenge at Selhurst Park that awaits the man who made his name at Brentford?

"It's going to be a bit of a shock for Thomas Frank," former West Ham and England goalkeeper Rob Green tells BBC Sport.

"He had his success at Brentford - a very well-run club where players are brought in with a lot of thinking and planning to take over the players they sell for profit.

"They lose players and then have a mad scramble to get players in. They have a team that has been decimated by sales and not replaced by the same quality.

"Thomas Frank needs to find something within that team that builds and garners the belief that means that they can compete in the Premier League, because it feels a long way short of that right now."

Will Frank prove the right fit for Palace and haul the Eagles out of the relegation zone?

Since getting the sack at Tottenham after 26 league games last season, Frank has been out of management longer than he was in charge of Spurs.

In the summer he released a statement in which he said "there have been conversations and opportunities" to return to management, but that he had "decided not to rush into the next role".

Frank's name was heavily linked with Palace before they went for a head coach with no Premier League experience to replace Oliver Glasner - the man who delivered an FA Cup, a Conference League title and the Community Shield before moving to Nottingham Forest.

"Palace had one of the best managers they have had, if not forever, silverware coming across the doorstep. Look at what they achieved last season and instead of building on that, they dismantled a team," said former Tottenham and England goalkeeper Paul Robinson.

Frank once described managing as being on a "hamster wheel" and a "crazy circus"., external

Palace confirmed his coaching staff will include current assistant manager Paddy McCarthy and goalkeeping coach Andy Quy, who previously worked with him at Brentford.

Justin Cochrane, who is part of Thomas Tuchel's England staff, is set to join.

Palace are also in the process of approaching Chelsea set-piece coach Bernardo Cueva, who would join as assistant first-team coach.

It is understood Frank would like to take Andreas Georgson from Tottenham, though the north London club are determined to keep the Swede.

Denmark fitness coach Chris Haslam, who worked with Frank at Tottenham, is another potential member of Palace's new coaching set-up.

A trip to Coventry City awaits Palace on Saturday.

So why does Frank feel now is the right moment to return to management at a club propping up the table?

Frank, who was part of BBC Sport's World Cup punditry team during the summer, will be coming into the job refreshed and with renewed energy and enthusiasm following several months out of the game.

Between his appointment as Brentford boss in October 2018 and the sack at Tottenham earlier this year, he managed without a break for seven years and four months.

Spending the past few months away from Premier League pressure has allowed Frank, in his own words, to "study, observe and learn from other leaders both within sport and beyond".

Will his positivity and passion rub off on a Palace team who have lost seven times in 10 top-flight matches?

Would Thomas Frank be a good fit for Crystal Palace?

Frank, who places a major emphasis on set-piece organisation, will have to hit the ground running at Palace, who have lost their past four league games.

They have conceded more goals than anyone else in the Premier League (24) and have scored only 10 themselves.

"If you want someone to go in and restore some stability and defensive solidity while improving the set-piece element of the team, then Thomas Frank is the perfect man for the job," Times football writer Tom Allnutt told BBC Radio 5 Live's Football Daily podcast.

With the Premier League season just 10 games old, Frank certainly has time to turn it around and will have targets in mind when the transfer window opens in January.

Palace sold France centre-back Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea for Â£52m and Colombia right-back Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest for Â£22m during the summer transfer window.

Allnutt added: "We know they have sold so many good players and so far I don't think they have really replaced them adequately."

Another challenge for Frank is getting midfielder Adam Wharton, who has not played for England since March, back to something like his best form.

These are all challenges the new manager will relish.

After his bruising experience at Tottenham - having established Brentford in the Premier League - Frank has decided to climb back on the hamster wheel with Palace.

"Crystal Palace and Thomas Frank feels like a very good fit," added Robinson.

Crystal Palace fan calls Thomas Frank 'the perfect hire'

Thomas Frank has a lot of work to do as Crystal Palace have undoubtedly been the worst team in the Premier League so far this season, ranking bottom not just in points (seven) but also goal difference (-14) and expected goal difference (-8.1).

It's the defence where Frank will have to focus most of his attention. Not only have Palace conceded the most goals (24) but they've also faced the most shots (189) and have the worst expected goals against (xGA) figure in the league (21.9).

Their attack has actually not been too bad. While only Hull have taken fewer shots, the Eagles have created really good chances and have perhaps been unlucky not to score a few more goals given the opportunities they've had.

There is also one significant factor in Frank's favour. Although Palace may be bottom of the Premier League, they are certainly not cut adrift as they sit just two points from safety.

The side propping up the table at this stage have had an average of just three points in the past 10 seasons, but for as bad as they've been, Palace have seven - the most the bottom side have had after 10 games for 24 years.

#806. Detroit Lions’ Aidan Hutchinson Out for the Remaining Season

Detroit Lions’ defensive end Aidan Hutchinson is out for the rest of the NFL season after he tore his ACL in an on-field celebration after sacking Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.

The Detroit Lions are down another member of the pride.

The NFL team’s defensive end Aidan Hutchinson is out for the season after he tore his ACL during an on-field celebration against the Patriots on Nov. 15.

In the first quarter of the game, which was played in Germany, Hutchinson sacked Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. The play, however, would prove disastrous for both players.

After the collision, Hutchinson leapt into the air in celebration. As he landed, however, the 26-year-old’s right knee buckled beneath him, and he collapsed to the ground. Though he was able to walk off the field with the assistance of the Lions’ training staff, Hutchinson didn’t return to the game.  The NFL Network Insider’s Ian Rapoport later confirmed on Nov. 16 that the player had torn his ACL, cutting his season short.

As for Maye, Rapoport also shared an update on the Patriots’ star, confirming the 24-year-old suffered a “significant lower leg injury,” believed to be a fractured ankle, during the sack. According to Rapoport, the injury could mean the 2025 NFL MVP runner-up is also out for the rest of the Patriots’ season.

Meanwhile, Hutchinson’s ligament tear is the second major injury to befall the Lions in the team’s 2026-2027 season, coming just two weeks after linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a severe neck injury against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 1.

The 26-year-old went down in the fourth quarter of the game after tackling T.J. Hockenson, resulting in a terrifying moment when Campbell was unable to move. He was treated by medical staff before being transported off the field on a stretcher to applause from fans and players.

In the time since, various members of the Lions team and staff have shared updates on how Campbell—dad to 4-month-old son Cooper with wife Megan Campbell—has been faring, including the player himself.

Just three days after he was hospitalized, Campbell shared an encouraging update on his progress, which he said had him feeling “incredibly encouraged.”

“I have full movement in my lower body,” Campbell shared in a statement to the Lions’ Instagram Nov. 4, “and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body.”

And though he acknowledged “there’s still work ahead,” he added, “I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.”

More recently, head coach Dan Campbell (no relation) confirmed he was in constant communication with his player.

“He is good spirits,” the coach shared following the match up against the Patriots. “And he continues to get better every day.”

For more insight into Campbell's health journey, read on.

Jack Campbell was injured during the Detroit Lions’ Nov. 1 game against the Minnesota Vikings

In the fourth quarter of the teams' match-up, Campbell tackled opponent T.J. Hockenson—his third tackle of the game—and was hit on the way down.

He lay face-down on the field, unable to move after the play, and had to be carried off on a backboard by medical personnel.

Campbell was rushed to a nearby hospital to have his neck evaluated

A reporter present at the game called Campbell’s hit the “scariest moment” he’d ever witnessed at Ford Field in a Nov. 1 post on X. He also confirmed that Campbell’s wife Megan Campbell and their baby boy Cooper, who was born in July 2026, were brought down to the field to accompany the player in an ambulance.

Lions coach Dan Campbell—who has no relation to the linebacker—said the team was “thinking about him” in a post-game interview, but had no information to share.

In a post on X following the game, the Detroit Lions confirmed that Campbell was brought “to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury.”

Campbell has remained hospitalized following his injury

On Nov. 2, the Detroit Lions confirmed that Campbell was being closely monitored at the hospital.

“Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital,” the team wrote in a post on X. “Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time.”

Lions coach says Campbell’s recovery update is “positive”

In a press conference one day after Campbell’s injury, Coach Campbell confirmed a heartening update on his player’s recovery.

“It’s positive,” he said. “Your prayers are working. Please continue to do that. We’ll leave it at that. Just continue to pray for him but it is positive news on Jack.”

Coach Campbell calls player an “unbelievable person”

While addressing his player’s injury, the Detroit Lions coach emphasized Campbell’s impact on the team, especially after he was tapped as team captain for this season.

“I don’t even know if I can put it into words,” Dan said during a press conference Nov. 2. “You get voted captain, that says a ton, especially with this group of guys that has been assembled. He earned every bit of that. He’s trustworthy, he’s dependable. He’d give you the shirt off his back. He’s just all heart, man. All effort."

As he put it, “There’s not a man on this team that doesn’t respect Jack Campbell and care about him,”

In an appearance on 97.1 The Ticket Radio Show Nov. 3, Coach Campbell shared an update on his player’s recovery.

“It’s not easy because he’s going to always be on our minds over here,” he said. “The good news is he is improving.”

Campbell breaks silence, says he is "very optimistic" about progress

The linebacker shared a positive update Nov. 4, noting he is "encouraged by the progress" he has made in the three days since his injury.

“I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body,” he wrote in a statement shared to the Detroit Lions' Instagram. "I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.”

#805. 'Don't panic': SpaceX pens familiar message on Starship ahead of historic double-catch test flight

Join The Club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.
